MPs have voted against a fresh move to legalise assisted dying in a dramatic U-turn after the legislation was revived in parliament on Friday.

The bill was voted down by a majority of 16, after 286 MPs voted against while 270 voted in favour, despite it having previously passed two votes in the House of Commons, in 2024 and 2025.

Under the proposed terms, terminally ill adults in England and Wales expected to live for under six months could have been able to request an assisted death, provided it receives authorisation from two medical practitioners alongside a specialist panel.

Although approved twice previously by the House of Commons, the measures stalled in the House of Lords this April. Proponents denounced a "denial of democracy" after peers submitted hundreds of amendments, effectively filibustering the proposed legislation.

Here we take a look at how we got here and what is to come.

open image in gallery Under the proposed terms, terminally ill adults in England and Wales expected to live for under six months could request an assisted death, provided it receives authorisation from two medical practitioners alongside a specialist panel ( Alamy/PA )

What happened today?

The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill was brought back in the Commons on Friday, with MPs delivering passionate speeches both in favour and against the legislation during a more than four-hour debate.

It is a private member’s Bill (PMB), also known as a backbench Bill, so is not government-backed.

The government has a neutral position on it, allowing MPs to vote according to their consciences, rather than along party lines.

What did MPs decide and what happens now?

In the second reading of the bill, put forward by Labour’s Lauren Edwards, MPs voted by 286 to 270 for the bill to be blocked.

It followed a number of emotional interventions from MPs across the House, with Labour MP Ashley Dalton - who has incurable metastatic breast cancer - urging colleagues to vote down the legislation.

It means the bill will not move forward for further debate in committee, debate and votes on amendments at report stage, and then another vote at what is known as Third Reading.

A bill to introduce assisted dying may return to parliament at some point in the future, with a bill potentially being reintroduced again by a private member’s bill, or by government legislation.

However, it is unlikely this will happen in the near future and could take years for another debate to take place, if ever.

What has the response been?

Campaigners against assisted dying welcomed the fall of the bill, which they described as a “victory for disabled people, terminally ill people, and everyone this bill would have put at risk”.

“As disabled people, we fight every day just to get support to eat, wash, leave our homes, and work, while palliative and social care systems remain dangerously underfunded,” campaign group Assist Us To Live said.

But campaigners in favour of assisted dying said the legislation’s failure to proceed is “devastating for dying people and their families”.

Sarah Wootton, chief executive of Dignity in Dying, said that while Parliament had rejected the legislation, assisted dying was inevitable and a question of “when, not if”.

“By refusing to send this bill back to the Lords, the House of Commons has endorsed the wrecking tactics of a handful of peers who stopped Kim Leadbeater’s Bill being considered properly in the first place,” she said

“It will be seen as a failure of our democracy that a Bill, supported by three quarters of the public, has been blocked in this way.

Amongst MPs, the response has been mixed.

A small group of MPs cheered and pumped their fists as MPs voted against the draft law, while others in favour of the bill expressed their disappointment.

Labour MP Jess Phillips, who is in favour of assisted dying, told The Independent: "I am devastated. But its not the end, it took many attempts to change abortion law, and so it will continue."

Former cabinet minister Liz Kendall said she was “deeply disappointed” to lose the vote, but insisted assisted dying “will happen eventually”.

“Because people deserve greater choice and control and to die with dignity & respect,” she said.

Did the Bill not run out of time earlier this year?

It did. The Bill, previously brought forward by Labour MP Kim Leadbeater, fell in April, having run out of time to become law before Parliament was prorogued that month, having effectively been talked out.

It had previously passed two votes in the House of Commons, in 2024 and 2025.

open image in gallery MPs will debate the legislation and a vote will likely take place mid-afternoon ( PA Archive )

The second vote saw the majority in favour of the Bill narrow to 23 from 55.

On that occasion, 14 MPs switched from voting in favour to against, with some arguing the dropping of the previously promised High Court judge safeguard had “drastically weakened” the proposals.

What happened in the House of Lords?

Peers faced accusations of filibustering – or delaying – the Bill after more than 1,200 amendments were put forward in the House of Lords, with more than 800 of those tabled or sponsored by seven peers.

Opponents at the time branded the Bill “hopelessly flawed” while supporters accused them of a “denial of democracy”.

So, how did it come back?

Labour MP Lauren Edwards reintroduced the Bill to Parliament.

She said people were “quite rightly frustrated by the process not being seen to conclusion in the last Parliament” and that she “felt a responsibility to those people who really wanted this legislation to be brought in”.

open image in gallery Prime minister Andy Burnham has already stated he will abstain from voting on the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill so as not to ‘unduly influence the debate’ ( PA Wire )

She has appealed to her colleagues in the Commons to vote for the bill “so that we can respect the will of the chamber and we can have it go through the usual processes in the House of Lords, just like any other form of legislation”.

What does the Bill propose?

The proposed legislation puts forward a change to the law allowing adults in England and Wales, with fewer than six months to live, to apply for an assisted death subject to the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.

open image in gallery Even if the Bill is approved, an implementation period has previously been agreed, meaning it could be four years after a law was passed before the first assisted death would take place ( PA )

What is the current law?

Assisted suicide is banned in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, with a maximum prison sentence of 14 years.

In Scotland, it is not a specific criminal offence but assisting the death of someone can leave a person open to being charged with murder or other offences.

What is happening with assisted dying in other nearby jurisdictions?

In March, legislation that would have made Scotland the first nation in the UK to back assisted dying was defeated at Holyrood.

Jersey’s States Assembly passed its draft Assisted Dying Law earlier this year and on July 9 it was granted royal assent.

Only certain sections of the law – allowing for the service’s set-up and the establishment of a committee to approve guidance – have come into force.

The parts allowing people to request assisted deaths have not yet come into force and it is expected the full law will be in place in autumn 2027, meaning that is the earliest the first assisted death could take place on the island.

The Isle of Man’s assisted dying Bill is now unlikely to get royal assent before October, despite the Tynwald becoming the first parliament across the UK and Crown Dependencies to agree a framework for assisted dying back in March 2025.

It is thought the implementation period for an assisted dying service to be in place could be up to two years after a law is in force, meaning it could be late 2028 by the time the first assisted death takes place on the island.

Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate from Michigan, responded after an audience member at the Republican midterm convention called for him to be “shot.”

The call to violence was heard as Senator Ted Cruz, a Texas Republican, addressed the Dallas crowd on the second night of the first-of-its-kind convention.

Cruz singled out three Democrats: Texas Senate candidate James Talarico, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and El-Sayed. After each line of criticism, a man in the audience could be heard yelling, “He should be shot!”

During an interview with CNN later on Thursday night, host Kaitlin Collins asked El-Sayed what went through his mind when he heard the interjection.

“Look, I’m a dad with two daughters, and I hope those daughters get to grow up and live with their dad,” the 41-year-old candidate said. “This is what has become norm in our politics. I mean, literally calls to violence and the inability for anybody to actually call it out.”

open image in gallery Democratic candidate for US Senate Abdul El-Sayed responded after an audience member at the Republican midterm convention called for him to be shot ( Getty Images )

“Democracy is supposed to be the process by which we solve our problems peacefully,” he continued. “We can learn to disagree agreeably, and when you hear that kind of call to violence, it should be shuddering to all of us. We have a responsibility to lower the temperature, to release that this is not a bloodsport, where you’re just trying to bash the other guy.”

El-Sayed added that he entered politics not to defeat Republicans but to solve problems, such as reforming the U.S. health care system.

“And so I hope that everybody who heard that is going to call it out for what it is — a call to violence that ought to be condemned across the board — and that we can actually turn our politics back into a conversation about what really matters,” he said.

open image in gallery Texas Senator Ted Cruz speaks at the Republican National Midterm Convention in Dallas when someone called for the people he was mentioning to be shot ( Reuters )

A representative for Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate running against El-Sayed, told CNN that Rogers “condemns those comments — and all political violence.”

Experts have warned that political violence is rising in the U.S., citing high-profile cases such as the assassination of Charlie Kirk, the killing of a Minnesota Democratic lawmaker and the multiple assassination attempts against President Donald Trump.

Recently, an armed man charged toward Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for Ohio governor, during a campaign event at a state fair, prosecutors said.

El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and progressive who supports Medicare for All, won the Democratic nomination last month. He will face off against Rogers, a former congressman, in the November 3 election.

Recent polls indicate it is shaping up to be a close race.

An Afghan woman who was accused of supporting an Islamic State-inspired plot in the United States and whose case was the first for an obscure and long-dormant court has been deported, the Justice Department said Friday.

Nazira Haji Zada was arrested in July at her Fort Worth, Texas, home and brought before the Alien Terrorist Removal Court on a Justice Department application to deport her from the U.S. On Friday, the department said that she had waived her rights to challenge her detention and had agreed to be deported.

It wasn't immediately clear when or to where she was deported.

The swift resolution averts what could have been a protracted legal fight testing the authority of the court, which was established in 1996 but until July had not received any petitions, as well as the strength of allegations against Haji Zada.

The Justice Department has described Haji Zada as a supporter of the Islamic State and identified her at the time as the mother and mother-in-law of two Afghan men who were convicted in Oklahoma of plotting an attack in the U.S. on Election Day in 2024. The plans were foiled before any attack took place.

Her lawyers at the time of the deportation had been pressing the court to force the Justice Department to share information and other evidence to support the allegations in the case.

The long-dormant court has specific authority to conduct deportation proceedings for people whom the Justice Department classifies as “alien terrorists.” The court is comprised of five federal judges from different districts across the country who are appointed by the U.S. chief justice.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: ‘All I see are dead bodies’: The survivors of Syria’s chemical massacres
News.content:
“Unfortunately, I am still alive,” says Mohammed Suliaiman Abo Alkair, his green eyes heavy and distant.

The 38-year-old steps from his living room onto the roof and gestures towards a cluster of trees – a lone patch of green in a sea of grey rubble. It was there, at two in the morning 13 years ago that the whistle of a rocket ended not in an explosion but a thud.

For a moment, there was relief; the feeling of being spared. But then came a cloud of the nerve agent sarin.

Almost everyone around Mohammed died. His family and one small boy in a neighbouring house were the only ones to survive.

That August night, as Damascus slept, forces loyal to the Syrian President Bashar al-Assad launched eight sarin-filled rockets at the opposition-held districts of Zamalka, Ein Tarma and Jobar. The US government estimated that 1,429 people were killed, including 426 children. Other estimates put the number at 1729.

For more than a decade, nobody was held to account. Mr Assad denied the attack, shielded those responsible and later used sarin again – at Khan Sheikhoun in 2017, and in at least ten further attacks documented by the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons.

Only after Mr Assad fled Syria in December 2024 did the prospect of justice emerge. Investigators for Syria’s new government have since uncovered previously undeclared chemical-munitions caches, and the authorities have detained 18 suspects. None has yet been tried or punished.

But as attention turns at last to justice, the survivors remain invisible, absent from the reckoning. For now at least they remain largely invisible.

News.title: What an AI Armageddon might actually look like
News.content:
Jacob Coxon has left AI developer Anthropic with a public reckoning. For three years, the 27-year-old Brit trained models at OpenAI and Anthropic.

Both AI startups acted irresponsibly, Coxon wrote on X on Wednesday. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Jacob Coxon warned.

The response from his manager arrived just hours later. Evan Hubinger, Head of Alignment Research at Anthropic, also confirmed the warning: “We are, in fact, earnestly convinced that AI could kill all humans! I think the probability of that happening within the next decade is greater than ten percent.”

Anthropic, he added, does not yet have a solution to this problem.

When the head of safety at a multibillion-dollar technology company casually predicts humanity’s downfall at the hands of his own product, the debate leaves the realm of academic thought experiments.

The warning comes from the engineers writing the code. Both developers point to an industry dynamic in which competitive pressures outweigh safety concerns.

But what exactly are AI developers afraid of? What is the hypothetical scenario in which artificial intelligence brings about Armageddon?

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

Sports.title: James Rodriguez, 35, signs for eighth club in six years after spending World Cup unemployed
Sports.content:
JAMES RODRIGUEZ has returned to play in Colombia ​for the first time since leaving ‌as a teenager.

The midfielder has joined Medellin giants Atletico Nacional on a free transfer.



The ​35-year-old most recently played for ​Minnesota United in the MLS.

Rodriguez has signed a contract with Atletico that ​runs until the summer of 2027.



The Colombian side ​will be the 14th club in a career that has taken Rodriguez to 12 countries.

He has now played for eight clubs in the past six years.



The Colombia captain led his country at the World Cup, and rolled back the years with some brilliant performances.

He has made 131 international appearances for the South American nation, with the highlight his Golden Boot in the 2014 tournament in Brazil.

In their announcement, Atletico said: “This isn’t an announcement. It is a labor of love for this team.

“It is the work of many people, day in and day out, done quietly to ensure Nacional grows ever greater.

Sports.title: Chelsea hand Pedro Neto new SIX-YEAR contract just weeks after being linked with Man City transfer exit
Sports.content:
PEDRO NETO is set to stay at Chelsea until at least 2032 under a fresh deal.

The Portuguese winger attracted interest from across Europe this summer, but the allure of Xabi Alonso convinced him to stay.



Neto, who will receive a pay rise, will also have the option of an extra year on top of his five-year agreement.

His Blues season got off to a flying start, already boasting five appearances and two goals in less than three weeks.



He said: “It’s an unbelievable moment. From when I arrived, I have always felt like the people here helped me a lot.

“I feel like home here, I feel like I want to achieve more things here.

“I’m really excited because I think we can achieve a lot of things together.”

Neto has been under the cosh as his new boss moulds him into a wing-back, but the Basque boss has been impressed so far.

Alonso said: “He has many qualities, he can play on the last line and defend on the first line.

“He has the capacity to do many things.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“He is good one-v-one, scoring goals, he has a fantastic work rate and connects very well with the players around.

“I knew him well from watching many Chelsea games. With him you know he is going to compete and you want these kinds of players in your team.

“I am very happy with Pedro and the work he is doing.”

While the 26-year-old was never taken off the transfer table this summer, his £100m price tag sent a bold message to lingering clubs.



He was even tipped for a move to Prem rivals Manchester City in the summer as former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca looked to bolster his ranks.

Joao Pedro, Reece James and Moises Caicedo have similarly agreed fresh deals with improved terms as Stamford Bridge looks to a new era under Alonso.

Neto joined the west London outfit for £51.4million from Wolves in 2024 and has since racked up a whopping 108 appearances, scoring 21 goals and providing 19 assists.

Sports.title: Exciting 28-goal striker, 22, at centre of international tug-of-war with major nations fighting for his first senior cap
Sports.content:
CLUB BRUGGE striker Nicolo Tresoldi is at the heart of a tug-of-war between Germany and Italy.

The 22-year-old has scored 28 club goals since the start of last season.



He is Italian by birth but grew up in Germany as a child and is therefore eligible to play for either nation.

In his youth career so far he has represented Germany at the Under-19, Under-20 and Under-21 levels.



New Italy manager Roberto Mancini wants the striker in his squad but, according to Gazzetta, the young forward is asking for more time to decide.

He reportedly wants to play in the U21 European Championship with Germany next summer before deciding which nation to represent at senior level.

Italy are thought to be unhappy waiting that long, and there is no guarantee they will resume talks with him.

The Azzurri have needed a top striker for a number of years.

Mancini rejoined Italy as manager less than two months ago, five years after winning the Euros with the country.

The 61-year-old wants Tresoldi in his squad, though it seems he will not be available for the Nations League games between September and October.

Mancini is being tasked with overseeing the return of Italy as one of the giants in international football.

The four-time World Cup winners have incredibly not competed in a World Cup since 2014.

Sports.title: Incredible INJURED XI that could win Premier League title including crocked Man Utd, Arsenal and Chelsea stars
Sports.content:
JUST four weeks into the new Prem season, physio rooms are already overflowing with crocked stars.

Some players were injured at the newly-extended World Cup, while others are still nursing major issues from last season.



With so many players out, English top flight clubs shelled out a record £3.5bn on new recruits.

If these forgotten stars could team up and get fit, they would make a formidable unit.



SunSport takes a look at the best XI Premier League stars yet to play a single minute this season.

Well, almost all Prem goalkeepers are fit and firing at the moment.

Ex-England stopper Jack Butland of Hull and Manchester United‘s Tom Heaton find themselves sidelined, with elbow and hamstring injuries respectively.

On account of having played more football in recent years, Butland gets the nod in our team.

The right of defence is made up of Arsenal duo Jurrien Timber and William Saliba.

Timber’s Champions League final cameo remains his only appearance since March, although he is nearing a return.

Chelsea new boy Marco Palestra fills in at left-back, having sustained a knock in training on the eve of the season.

Palestra’s Chelsea team-mate Jordan Henderson is in midfield, still sidelined by the freak broken wrist he suffered at the World Cup.



The England veteran partners Man Utd summer signing Carlos Baleba, who is yet to debut for his new side due to an ankle issue.

It’s a Spurs duo on the wings, with long-term absentees Xavi Simons and Dejan Kulusevski on the left and right respectively.

Kulusevski, meanwhile, has been out for 488 days with a knee injury sustained before Tottenham’s victorious Europa League final.

Sports.title: Why Man Utd winning Champions League game vs Sabah is BAD OMEN for Manchester derby vs City due to spooky curse
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED go into Sunday’s Manchester derby fresh off the back of a comfortable win in the Champions League, but that could prove to be a bad omen.

Michael Carrick saw his side cruise to a 4-0 win on Old Trafford‘s return to the Champions League after three seasons away.



However, a fan theory doing the rounds on social media suggests the Red Devils could now be at a disadvantage going into one of their biggest games of the season.

The theory is that Man Utd perform better in big games when the odds are stacked against them and the pressure cooker is cranked up to maximum.



And perhaps worryingly for Sunday’s hosts, there is some weight to that theory.

Looking at the last 15 Manchester derbies, excluding the Community Shield, Man Utd have won just five.

Of those five, only three have seen victory over the Cityzens after a win the game before.

The last time this happened was in December 2024, when Man Utd beat Viktoria Plzen in the Europa League before beating City 2-1 at the Etihad.

On the other hand, Man Utd have been on the losing side SIX times after winning the game beforehand.

This happened as recently as last season, when Man Utd beat Burnley 3-2 before they were thrashed 3-0 by City days later.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But only once have they beaten City having lost the game before, that being the most recent derby when they won 2-0 at Old Trafford following their 2-1 defeat to Brighton in the FA Cup.

Man Utd have also just once beaten City following a draw in the last 15 meetings, that coming in 2021 when they followed up a 0-0 draw against Crystal Palace with a 2-0 win away at the Etihad.

The Old Trafford outfit have played City once following a Champions League game in this sample size too.

That was their 2-2 draw against Atalanta in 2021, before they lost 2-0 at home to Pep Guardiola‘s side at home.

Going into Sunday’s clash, City are looking to maintain their 100 per cent winning start in the league under new boss Enzo Maresca.



Meanwhile, Man Utd have endured a stuttering start after losing to Hull, beating Ipswich and then drawing at Everton.

They can take solace going into the derby that their wins this season have all come in front of their own fans, and will hope to repeat that despite history suggesting they might have needed a boot up the backside to propel them into gear.

Sports.title: Lucas Bergvall performs major U-turn by signing new Tottenham deal just months after exit push and late Chelsea interest
Sports.content:
LUCAS BERGVALL has performed a big U-turn by signing a bumper new deal with Spurs – just months after telling the club he was open to leaving.

The Swedish star, 20, was worried back then about his development and opportunities in his favoured No8 position, especially after Spurs splashed £185million on midfielders Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.



Bergvall also was left frustrated at the lack of communication about his career path from the club.

But a productive chat with boss Roberto De Zerbi over pre-season put his mind at rest and now Bergvall has committed his future with fresh terms.



Spurs never wanted to lose the talented youngster and rejected bids from Newcastle and Nottingham Forest over the summer.

Chelsea were also given short shrift when showing late interest in the window too.

The 14-cap Sweden international said: “I think we’re building something great here. It’s an exciting time for the club and that’s why I’m happy to extend my contract.

“I’m always trying to achieve as much as possible, to be the best version of myself both on and off the pitch and I know this is the right place to do that.

“Personally, my goal is to produce more for the team – performances, goals and assists – to help as much as I can. I’m getting better every day in training and I’m looking forward to what will be a really good season ahead.”

Europa League winner Bergvall has 80 appearances for Spurs and started the first game of the season at Brentford.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

It showed how much he remains in De Zerbi’s plans, although the Swede was replaced at half-time after losing the ball for the Bees’ second goal in the 3-0 defeat.

Bergvall follows the likes of Micky van de Ven, Pedro Porro and Antonin Kinsky in signing new deals in the last few months.

Boss De Zerbi added: “Every day in training you can see Lucas’ desire to learn, improve and push himself to the highest level.

“Lucas is brave, he wants responsibility and has the personality to play in big moments. He also understands that development is a process and he has shown a fantastic attitude towards working on the areas of his game where he can become even better.

“I believe his best football is still ahead of him and we want to give Lucas the platform to reach his full potential.”

Sports.title: Best starts to the season EVER as Arsenal look to smash Chelsea’s 21-year-old record and continue incredible winning run
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have enjoyed a flying start in their bid to win their first ever back-to-back Premier league titles.

The Gunners finally broke their duck last season by winning their first Prem trophy since the Invincibles’ 2004 triumph.



And the North Londoners have won all three of their opening matches this term in the English top flight.

The same, though, goes for Manchester City in their first season without Pep Guardiola, as his successor Enzo Maresca is eyeing to break his mentor’s own record just three months into the job.



Nevertheless, both Arsenal and City have a long way to go to beat Chelsea’s 21-year-old record.

SunSport take you through all the best Premier League starts with the teams that registered the most wins in a row…



6 Wins: Manchester City – 2023/24

As mentioned earlier, Enzo Maresca has made a flying start to his first season as the replacement of Pep Guardiola, who took Manchester City to their greatest ever heights during a glittering ten-year reign.

Among Guardiola’s many achievements, is equalling City’s greatest ever Premier League start three years ago with wins over Burnley, Newcastle, Sheffield United, Fulham, West Ham and Nottingham Forest.

That led to a record fourth successive Prem title for Man City, which was also the Catalan tactician’s last before leaving last summer.



6 Wins: Liverpool – 2018/19

Liverpool came extremely close to finally winning their first ever Premier League title during the 2018/19 season.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Reds picked up wins over West Ham, Crystal Palace, Brighton, Leicester, Tottenham and Southampton.

The Merseysiders took things to the wire but missed out to the title to Manchester City in the final game of the season and accumulated 97 points – the highest return by a team to not win the English title – just one short of the top.

6 Wins: Manchester City – 2016/17

Pep Guardiola equalled his own record during the 2023/24 season from seven years before.



Manchester City defeated Sunderland, Stoke, West Ham, rivals Manchester United, Bournemouth and Swansea.

But despite the impressive start, City finished third with 15 points adrift of champions Chelsea.

6 Wins: Chelsea – 2009/10

Chelsea enjoyed a record-breaking season during the 2009/10 campaign under Carlo Ancelotti.



The Blues defeated Hull, Sunderland, Fulham, Burnley, Stoke and Tottenham in their first six Premier League matches.

Although that wasn’t the West Londoners’ longest streak, it did lead to the title and Carlo Ancelotti’s side became the first Prem team to score over 100 goals and the first top-flight club since Spurs in 1962/63.

6 Wins: Newcastle – 1994/95

Newcastle registered their best ever Premier League start under the late great Kevin Keegan.

The Magpies kicked things off with big wins over Leicester, Coventry, Southampton, West Ham, Chelsea and Arsenal.

Despite that record, though, the Toon couldn’t win their first ever Prem title and finished sixth – the worst final standing for any side with such a flawless start since 1992.



8 Wins: Liverpool – 2019/20

Liverpool finally won their inaugural Premier League honour and first title since 1990 after a 30-year wait in 2020.

And the signs were there for everyone to see as they defeated Norwich, Southampton, Arsenal, Burnley, Newcastle, Chelsea, Sheffield United and Leicester in their first eight matches.

Jurgen Klopp‘s side couldn’t equal Chelsea’s record as they then drew 1-1 with rivals Manchester United.



But they then embarked on a stunning 18-match winning run to have have an incredible 26 out of their first 27 games.

79 points out of 81.

Unsurprisingly after the Covid shutdown, the Reds became the Premier League’s most convincing ever winners.

9 Wins: Chelsea – 2005/06

Chelsea set the record in Jose Mourinho‘s second Premier League season with victories over Wigan, Arsenal, West Brom, Tottenham, Sunderland, Charlton, Aston Villa, Liverpool and Bolton.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

That led to the Blues’s first and only back-to-back Prem honours with 29 wins and only five losses in 38 matches.

The West Londoners were just two wins short from equalling the all-time record – set up before the revamped competition in 1992 – established by Tottenham during the 1960/61 season, while Manchester United also started the 1985/86 campaign with ten consecutive victories.

Sports.title: Chelsea and Man Utd icon Juan Mata makes final decision on playing future after becoming co-owner of Australian club
Sports.content:
JUAN MATA has bowed out of playing, just months after becoming a co-owner of Aussie club Melbourne Victory.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United star has opted to focus on his role in the A-League side’s ownership group.



Victory announced the final decision on Friday as Mata walks after spending only a single season as a club player.

A statement read: “After careful consideration, the 38-year-old, whose on-pitch contribution represented one of the most impressive individual seasons in A-Leagues history, will now concentrate his expertise with Victory on his position in the Club’s ownership group.”



The club added that Mata will consider the next steps of his career from his home in Europe.

He will also become chairman of Victory’s brand new football committee.



Mata arrived at AAMI Park in September 2025 and went on to win the Johnny Warren Medal as the best player in the A-League.

He also won Victory’s own player of the season award and was named in the PFA Team of the Season.

And the Spaniard even helped the Victoria club reach a 15th Finals Series.

Victory director of football John Didulica said: “Juan’s 2025/26 season will live long in the memory of Victory fans and should be cherished by all supporters of the world’s game here in Australia.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Mata said: “I loved every minute and so greatly enjoyed everything that we achieved last season, falling back in love with football at such a special place, in an amazing city that it was a privilege to call home.”

“Now I am excited about our next chapters, believing together in the future of Australian football and inspiring the next generation of Melbourne Victory players and supporters.”

Mata became a shareholder in Victory earlier this year and will now take on a bigger role behind the scenes.

He already has stakes in Alpine’s Formula One team and MLS side San Diego FC.



The midfielder spent four years at Chelsea before joining Manchester United in 2014.

He won the Champions League, Europa League and FA Cup during his time in England, as well as the 2010 World Cup and Euro 2012 with Spain.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick responds to Elliot Anderson's 'Kings of Manchester' jibe
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick responds to Elliot Anderson's 'Kings of Manchester' jibe

The Manchester United manager would never use the City midfielder's phrase but he knows victory in the derby would be just the start of his side's bid to become regular title challengers

View 4 Images Michael Carrick believes expectation has increased at Old Trafford

By Michael Carrick’s deadpan standards, he was almost a picture of animation when he was reminded of Elliot Anderson’s signing-on comments. “I’m definitely not using that phrase, at all, no,” the Manchester United manager laughed.

‌



When Anderson’s £116million move to the Etihad was confirmed in July, the England midfielder said he was particularly looking forward to playing against United. And here was his reason.

‌



“It’s been one of the biggest derbies in the world. And for as long as I’ve known, City have been the Kings of Manchester.”

‌



And just to wind up United further, City’s official website made it a capital K for Kings. An old school manager would have Anderson’s comments pinned on the dressing-room wall ahead of Sunday’s game.

Darren Fletcher confronts 'abusive' Man Utd fan as tempers flare at Old Trafford READ MORE :

Lisandro Martinez trolls Jamie Carragher as Man Utd star leaves Micah Richards in hysterics READ MORE :

And maybe Carrick will. After all, his first game in this permanent stint as United manager was a 2-0 victory over Pep Guardiola’s City at a raucous Old Trafford.

And City’s superiority in this fixture has not been eye-catchingly emphatic over the past decade. Of the last 20 Premier League meetings between the clubs, City have won 10, United have won seven, and there have been three draws.

‌



But City’s overall superiority HAS been emphatic. The last time United finished above City in the Premier League was at the end of the 2012-13 season.

View 4 Images Elliot Anderson says he has only known an era of Manchester City dominance (Image: Molly Darlington)

Elliot Anderson was ten years of age, so you know where he is coming from. Since then, City have won seven Premier League titles, three FA Cups, seven League Cups, a Champions League and a Club World Cup.

‌



In that time, United have won two FA Cups, two League Cups and a Europa League. No wonder Anderson knows City as the Kings of Manchester.

And Carrick is sensible enough to know that while his triumph over City earlier this year was hugely enjoyable, the ultimate target is an overall power shift. United need to join City as perennial title challengers.

“I understand it,” he said, expanding on Anderson’s remark. “We are humble enough and realistic enough to know where we have come from in recent history.

‌



View 4 Images Michael Carrick was successful in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford in January (Image: Getty Images)

“It is good, in a way, that expectation has shifted. All of a sudden, there are different things asked of us to maybe what was asked of us a few months ago.

“We are in the Champions League - that in itself shows the steps we have made. Now, it is about the next stage. We need to, and want to be better, and we want to be challenging more. That’s where we're at. It doesn't mean that we can't and we won't. It means we still hope, we believe, and we expect that we can be and we should be, but I understand the bigger picture.”

‌



And the bigger picture will be impacted by this latest derby, City already holding a five-point advantage over their neighbours in the Premier League table. Carrick, though, seemed bullish ahead of the meeting with Enzo Maresca’s men, saying: “I thought they (City) were very professional against Porto the other night.

View 4 Images Enzo Maresca has won his first four matches as Manchester City manager (Image: Dave Howarth - CameraSport via Getty Images)

"They are a very good team. We know we have to put in a good performance and do a lot of things right to get a result.

‌



“I think we have built up confidence over a period of time. I feel like we are getting better all the time and that helps us. It is is a big game, it is an important game, there is a lot riding on it.

“We are looking forward to it. We have got a short space of time to recover and prepare for it, but we will make the most of it.”

Sports.title: Behdad Eghbali's net worth compared to Premier League rivals ahead of full Chelsea takeover
Sports.content:
Behdad Eghbali's net worth compared to Premier League rivals ahead of full Chelsea takeover

This is how Behdad Eghbali's net worth stacks up to other Premier League owners

View 3 Images Behdad Eghbali could be nearing a complete takeover at Chelsea (Image: PA)

Chelsea are nearing a new dawn with Behdad Eghbali solely at the helm of the Premier League giants. Alongside Todd Boehly, the billionaire co-founder of Clearlake Capital were behind a consortium of investors to buy the west London side in 2022 for £4.25billion.

‌



Four years on from the purchase, the Iranian-American billionaire is closing in on full control of the football club. Reports emerged last month that negotiations had begun for Boehly, Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss to sell their shared 38.5% of Chelsea to Clearlake and Bloomberg now reports that a deal is nearing completion following an acceleration in talks in recent weeks.

‌



The potential sale would increase Eghbali and his firm's share in the club from 61.5% to 99.9%. According to Forbes, Eghbali, 50, has a net worth of £2.8bn, but even that staggering figure pales in comparison to some of the richest owners in the English top-flight.

‌



Standing at the top of the monetary conversation in the Premier League top-flight are Newcastle United's owners, the Public Investment Fund. The sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia tips the scale at £1.2trillion, with Liverpool's ownership combination of Fenway Sports Group (FSG) and Jeff Bezos' backed consortium possessing a net worth of £265bn in second place.

The new investment group at Anfield is headed by former QPR owner Amit Bhatia, who is the son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mitta, whose net worth sits at around £22bn. The Amazon founder is the third-richest individual in the world and has a net worth of £198bn.

Todd Boehly era at Chelsea nearly over with talks accelerating for duo to sell shares READ MORE :

Manchester City's Sheikh Mansour used to reign supreme at the top of the Premier League rich list, but now sits third with his personal wealth sitting at £20bn. Minority City shareholders Silver Lake take City's ownership value to £24bn.

‌



Sir Jim Ratcliffe's fortune is estimated at £15.2bn by the Sunday Times Rich List, with the Manchester United co-owner's wealth sitting higher than his business partners in the Glazer Family. According to Forbes, the long-time United owners have a net worth of £8.9bn.

View 3 Images Behdad Eghabli is set to complete a complete takeover at Chelsea (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Sports magnate Stan Kroenke has enjoyed numerous successes within his sporting portfolio, namely Arsenal's Premier League triumph last season. The American, who also owns the Los Angeles Rams, the Denver Nuggets and the Colorado Rapids, has a remarkable wealth estimated at £20.4bn.

‌



Forbes Real-Time Net Worth has Fulham owner Shahid Khan boasting a fortune of £14bn that he first built through Flex-N-Gate, a motor vehicles company. On top of his ownership of the Cottagers, the billionaire also owns NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Everton's ownership switched hands in 2024 when the Friedkin Group, led by American billionaire Dan Friedkin, completed a majority acquisition of the Toffees. The 61-year-old - who also owns Serie A giants Roma - has a net worth of £9.4bn.

Aston Villa are owned by V Sports, led by Nassef Sawiris and Wes Edens. The Egyptian billionaire's net worth sits at £7bn, while Edens - who also co-owns NBA side Milwaukee Bucks - boasts a £1.7bn fortune.

Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis has a net worth of around £5.18bn, according to Forbes, which lists Tottenham's Joe Lewis as having the same wealth.

Sports.title: Hull City were warned about road before Sorba Thomas overturned car outside training ground
Sports.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Hull City were warned about road before Sorba Thomas overturned car outside training ground

Hull City's £10.5million summer signing Sorba Thomas was involved in a collision outside the club's training ground, five days after the club were urged to warn new players about the road

View 4 Images Sorba Thomas' car overturned in the crash (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

A local councillor says he asked Hull City to warn their new players of the dangers of the road outside their training ground just days before Sorba Thomas' crash.

‌



Thomas, who joined Hull from Stoke on transfer deadline day in a £10.5million deal, was involved in a collision on Millhouse Woods Lane on Friday morning, remarkably escaping the scene "completely unscathed".

‌



The residential road is just a stone's throw from Hull's training ground. Two other cars were damaged in the incident. Hull issued a statement to "reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed."

‌



Meanwhile, Humberside Police confirmed they were "in attendance following reports of a road traffic collision" and advised motorists to avoid the area. The incident comes the day before Hull face Chelsea in the Premier League at Stamford Bridge and the proximity of the crash to the training ground meant their team coach was delayed in leaving for London.

4 View 4 Images Two other cars were damaged in the incident (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw) 4 View 4 Images Sorba Thomas car was towed away after the crash (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

‌



Local councillor Phil Redshaw visited the scene of the crash on Friday. He told The Mirror there have been “a few near misses” recently down the road in Cottingham, a suburb of Hull.

He added: “I wrote to the Hull City club secretary on Sunday asking them to remind players to be careful driving down the road because of the residents’ concerns. I wanted them to remind their staff to drive with extra care, because they get new players in every season.”

Hull City referred to their statement when asked about councillor Redshaw's comments.

‌



Redshaw says he visited residents of Millhouse Woods Lane on Friday to warn them about the dangers of the road, with gardens backing directly onto the pavement where “lorries have no option but to go" in order to get past.

View 4 Images The £10.5m winger escaped the wreckage unhurt (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

Thomas was one of 17 new players to sign for Hull this summer following their promotion to the Premier League via the Championship play-offs. The Tigers were the busiest club in the Premier League this summer, with their 17 incomings the most of any side, while their net spend of £160m put them fourth in the division.

‌



The 27-year-old Wales international has made two appearances for The Tigers so far, making his Premier League debut in the goalless draw with Aston Villa on the weekend before starting in the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday night.

Hull have made a brilliant start to the top-flight campaign, keeping three successive clean sheets to beat Manchester United and Coventry and draw with Villa. Sergej Jakirovic's side sit third in the Premier League table ahead of their trip to Stamford Bridge for Saturday's 3pm kick-off.

Sports.content:
England U21s all-time top goalscorer asked to change allegiance despite senior cap

One Premier League star could soon be changing his international allegiance

View 2 Images Eddie Nketiah is the all-time top goalscorer for England U21s (Image: (Photo by Marc Atkins/Getty Images))

England U21s' all-time leading goalscorer Eddie Nketiah is reportedly in talks to change his international allegiance despite already receiving a senior cap for the Three Lions. The Crystal Palace striker has one senior appearance for England, making his bow against Australia in a friendly in October 2023.

‌



The 27-year-old, former Arsenal striker, is the all-time leading goalscorer for England U21s with 16 goals in 17 games for the young Three Lions. However, The Standard claims Ghana has now initiated talks with the striker to convince him to change allegiances.

Nketiah is reportedly considering his next step and deciding whether or not to represent his parents' country of birth or hold out for further England caps.

Bruno Fernandes injury scare as Man Utd star seen 'limping' ahead of Manchester derby READ MORE :

The Crystal Palace forward is still eligible to represent Ghana, due to current FIFA regulations. They state a player cannot switch to another nation if they have played in more than three competitive senior games.

The Black Stars are looking to add more Premier League quality to their ranks, with the likes of Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo and Coventry midfielder Caleb Yirenkyi representing Ghana.

Nketiah has made a bright start to life under new Eagles boss Pierre Sage, starting all three of their top-flight games this season.

However, it's fair to say that he's struggled for goals since his move to Selhurst Park, managing just four in 19 appearances last season, down from the seven goals he scored in his first year at the club.

View 2 Images Crystal Palace striker Eddie Nketiah could play for Ghana in the future (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking about his start to life under Sage this season, Nketiah said: "I think the team are a bit more on the front foot, I would say.

"We want to press higher, be a bit more aggressive. I think obviously it's a different style, though it's the same system.

"It's a bit of a different style than we played last year, but I've enjoyed it. I think he [Sage] is really demanding – and not just him, all the coaching staff, the players…

"The quality of training has increased. I think everyone's up for it in these short, intense sessions.

"I think it's going to put us in good stead for the games coming up, and I'm sure we can start to pick up some points and climb up the table."

Sports.title: Premier League star flips car onto roof in terrifying incident as club release statement
Sports.content:
Hull City say new signing Sorba Thomas is "completely unscathed" after flipping his car onto its roof in a terrifying crash.

Pictures on social media on Friday morning showed his Land Rover Defender upside down on a residential street, with a member of the club's staff, understood to be manager Sergej Jakirovic, at the scene. The incident happened at around 9am on Millhouse Woods Lane, close to Hull's training ground.

Hull said in a statement: "Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground.

"The club is aware of images of Sorba’s car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed."

‌

Humberside Police said in a statement: "Officers and emergency services are currently in attendance following reports of a road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane, Cottingham at around 9am on Friday, 11 September 2026.

"The road remains closed and motorists are advised to avoid the area to allow emergency services to operate effectively."

‌



The incident happened in a quiet residential road with a 30mph speed limit in Cottingham, on the outskirts of Hull, and a stone's throw away from Hull's training ground.

View 6 Images Sorba Thomas car was towed away after the crash (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

Thomas' car has since been towed away, freeing up Millhouse Woods Lane just in time for the Hull City team coach, which is taking the squad down to London for their Premier League match against Chelsea on Saturday.

Phil Redshaw, a local councillor, visited the scene on Friday morning and said two parked cars, a blue Mini and a black 4x4, had also been damaged.

‌



He told The Mirror there have been “a few near misses” on the road recently and says lorries and coaches are forced to drive onto the pavement to get past.

View 6 Images A Mini was among the cars damaged (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

He added: “I wrote to the Hull City club secretary on Sunday asking them to remind players to be careful driving down the road because of the residents’ concerns. I wanted them to remind their staff to drive with extra care, because they get new players in every season.”

Land Rover Defenders are a favourite of footballers and can cost up to £160,000.

‌



View 6 Images The crash initially blocked the Hull City coach (Image: Cllr Phil Redshaw)

Wales international Thomas joined The Tigers from Stoke on transfer deadline day for £10.5million. The 27-year-old winger has made two appearances for his new club, in the 0-0 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League and the 1-0 defeat by Sunderland in the Carabao Cup.

Hull are preparing to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League at 3pm on Saturday. Jakirovic's side have made a brilliant start to the campaign following their promotion via the Championship play-offs, beating Manchester United and Coventry before drawing with Aston Villa to occupy third place.

View 6 Images Sorba Thomas has 27 caps for Wales (Image: Ian Cook/Getty Images)

‌



Jakirovic spoke about Thomas in his pre-match press conference on Thursday ahead of the trip to west London. "I don't have any doubt about Sorba because he made a difference in the Championship," he said.

"He is a left winger and we can use him inside like a left (sided) number 10. He knows football. He is very good in delivery and his end product is good. Also, he has very good set-pieces.

"He is sharp and has speed. Also, in defence, he is very responsible. I think he suits us a lot. Like always, I hope he can help us."

View 6 Images Sorba Thomas has only made two appearances for Hull City (Image: George Wood/Getty Images)

‌



Thomas was named as Stoke's Player of the Year last season after contributing 10 goals and 13 assists in all competitions. His departure to Hull on deadline day caused a stir at the club, with sporting director Jon Walters forced to address the situation in a statement.

“Although we are naturally disappointed with the way it has ended after just one season, I do understand that Sorba had an opportunity to play in the Premier League which, over the past few days, he has expressed a firm desire to take," he said. “We all thank him for his efforts last season and wish him well for the future.”

Sports.title: Lisandro Martinez trolls Jamie Carragher as Man Utd star leaves Micah Richards in hysterics
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez trolls Jamie Carragher as Man Utd star leaves Micah Richards in hysterics

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was in a playful mood after the Red Devils' 4-0 win over Sabah in the Champions League, delivering a cheeky dig at Jamie Carragher on CBS Sports

View Image Lisandro Martinez joked about Jamie Carragher (Image: CBS Sports)

Lisandro Martinez raised the roof with a cheeky joke that he only watches "quality players" when asked by Micah Richards who the best CBS Sports presenter was. Manchester United were successful in their Champions League opener with Sabah on Thursday, running out 4-0 winners at home.

‌



Michael Carrick's men clicked into gear at Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko and Martinez but Sabah to the sword. It was a night to remember for Martinez in particular, considering he bagged his first goal at Old Trafford.

‌



The centre-half was in a mischievous mood in the aftermath, as he joined the CBS set-up of Richards, Jamie Carragher, Thierry Henry and Kate Scott for a post-game interview. And when Richards asked who his favourite host was, the Argentine couldn't resit but have a cheeky jab.

‌



Jamie Carragher warns Michael Carrick he faces same problem as Gareth Southgate READ MORE :

Having singled out Henry as his top pick, Carragher asked: "What about us defenders?" which prompted a brilliantly sharp comeback from the 28-year-old. He said: "I watch quality players, you know?"

The quip brought the house down in the studio, with Henry, Carragher and Richards erupting in laughter and applause. The banter continued from there, with Martinez - a man of few words at the best of times - seizing the opportunity to take another dig at Carragher.

When Richards asked whether he used to watch the former Liverpool defender, and what he thought of him as a player, Martinez replied: "As a player? Good person you know," sending the studio into fits of laughter once more.

‌



It follows Carragher casting doubt over Martinez as a centre-half shortly after his arrival at the club in 2022, given the powerhouse stands at just 5ft9'. Speaking on Sky Sports at the time, the 48-year-old said: "We should never judge managers or players too early, but I'm convinced this can't work because the size of him playing in a back four.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta 'close to signing' new Arsenal contract despite one move interesting him
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta 'close to signing' new Arsenal contract despite one move interesting him

Mikel Arteta has transformed Arsenal since first taking charge in December 2019 and the Gunners boss has a decision to make, with his current deal set to expire in June

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is poised to sign a new contract with Arsenal (Image: Filippo MONTEFORTE / AFP via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is close to agreeing a new contract with Arsenal, despite being tempted by a return to Spain some time in the future. Arteta's current deal expires in nine months and the Gunners are keen to tie their manager down to fresh terms.

‌



The 44-year-old has transformed the club's fortunes since taking charge in December 2019, securing their first Premier League title in 22 years in May, as well as lifting the FA Cup and reaching the Champions League final.

‌



The Gunners are the firm favourites for the Premier League title this season and club chiefs understandably want to remove any doubt or speculation over Arteta's future. His last contract extension came back in September 2024 and only runs until the end of June.

‌



All parties are on the same page, with Arteta ready to put pen to paper on a contract which will establish him as one of the best-paid managers in the world. BBC Sport reports that negotiations have progressed in recent weeks and Arteta will improve his current terms, which are worth £10million per season, plus a £5m bonus for Champions League qualification.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



While there is currently no doubt about Arteta's commitment in north London, Arsenal are aware that he could one day be tempted by a return to his native Spain. However, one of the things in Arsenal's favour is the fact that Arteta would not be able to have as much of a say in every facet of the club were he to join Real Madrid or Barcelona.

The mutual respect is such now that Arteta has significant influence in Arsenal's transfer business. It was he who led the charm offensive in their attempts to lure Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior and Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez to Arsenal this summer.

Speaking last month about contract talks, Arteta said: "They (the fans) don't have to worry about any of that because I want to be here, I'm extremely happy and I feel very grateful to work with the people I work with. When we have the possibility, we will resolve that. That's it.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is very happy at Arsenal (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

"Everybody feels comfortable that the timing of the contract is not going to be an issue because my will certainly is to be here and I'm very happy here. My feeling from the club is the same one. That's why everyone is doing things in a very organic way."

That feeling is mutual, with the club's chief executive Richard Garlick saying recently that it was a "matter of time" before a new long-term deal was confirmed for Arteta.

Sports.title: Darren Fletcher cheered as 'abusive Man Utd fan' put in place after Champions League win
Sports.content:
Darren Fletcher cheered as 'abusive Man Utd fan' put in place after Champions League win

Manchester United icon Darren Fletcher put an abusive fan in their place after the Champions League win over Sabah FK

View 3 Images Man Utd icon Darren Fletcher put a fan in his place after the Sabah game. (Image: _StrettyEnd/X)

Manchester United icon Darren Fletcher was cheered by supporters after putting an abusive fan in his place following the win over Sabah FK in the Champions League on Thursday night. Michael Carrick's side made light work of the Azerbaijan outfit, running out 4-0 winners on home soil.

‌



Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko, and Lisandro Martinez were all on the scoresheet to kick start United's Champions League campaign. However, not everyone was happy after the game.

‌



One fan was reportedly being abusive towards the players as they made their way home after the game, and Fletcher wasted no time in putting the fan in their place.

‌



Bruno Fernandes injury scare as Man Utd star seen 'limping' ahead of Manchester derby READ MORE :

Michael Carrick gives Luke Shaw injury update after he misses game before Manchester derby READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

In footage shared on social media, the former United midfielder can be heard saying: "Hey, listen, it doesn't matter, you can't speak like that," before pointing at the fan.

Fletcher is cheered by the United fans in attendance before the former interim head coach says: "You're the reason people don't sign."

‌



3 View 3 Images Man Utd coach Darren Fletcher put an abusive fan in their place after the game against Sabah. (Image: _StrettyEnd/X) 3 View 3 Images Manchester United defeated Sabah FK on their return to the Champions League. (Image: (Photo by Zohaib Alam/Manchester United via Getty Images))

The United fans in the vicinity cheered once more before chanting 'Fletcher, Fletcher, Fletcher' as the coach made his way back to his car.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

United boss, Carrick, was pleased with his side's display against Sabah, and when asked if he felt the result was a perfect return to the Champions League, he said: "Yeah, I think so. Kind of what we set out to achieve, really.

"I think it was a good performance, individually, collectively, pretty much all the way through the game, from start to finish.

‌



"Boys that started, boys that came on the pitch, clean sheet, some goals and some good, exciting football. It was a good night all round."

However, there were causes for concern for the United boss, with captain Bruno Fernandes appearing to limp as he made his way home from Old Trafford.

The Portuguese midfielder was caught on camera departing the stadium alongside United staff, moving gingerly as he acknowledged supporters before making his way home.

Article continues below

Fernandes played the full 90 minutes in the Champions League clash, appearing fine throughout, suggesting any concern is likely to be minor. United will hope that's the case with a match against arch-rivals Man City on Sunday afternoon.

Sports.title: Inside the Solheim Cup: How players embraced 'insane' first-tee experience
Sports.content:
Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist said that the Solheim Cup first tee would be 'the place to be in the golfing world,' with that pre-tournament assessment spot on as she witnessed a spectacle unlike any other in the women's game.

The horseshoe-shaped grandstand around the first tee at Bernardus Golf was close to capacity long before daylight, with nearly 3,000 spectators - and plenty more along the fairway - creating a party-like atmosphere of noise and excitement.

United States captain Angela Stanford danced onto the tee after emerging from the tunnel, a walk Charley Hull said earlier in the week was like 'entering an arena', with vice-captains - from both sides - doing their best to make things even louder.

One sign on display read 'Dutch courage, European glory', with the Netherlands doing the players proud by creating a boisterous environment more akin to a football stadium or darts event than a golf course.

Nordqvist's vice-captain Anne van Dam grabbed the microphone to guide the crowd through "Links Rechts", the song that became the unofficial anthem for the Dutch football team during the World Cup and involves lots of bouncing in a certain direction.

"It doesn't get better than this," Nordqvist said about the atmosphere. "The crowds are amazing. I don't think I've ever seen this many Europeans on the first tee."

Image: Costumes linked to both teams were on display in a colourful grandstand

Stands full of fans dressed in banana costumes, stars and stripes suits and golf bucket hats all jumping together at 7.20am was a brilliantly bonkers scene, with the dancing and singing only increasing as they edged closer to play getting under way.

"Let's go Europe, let's go!" chants echoed around the grandstand before Europe's classic 'Final Countdown' blasted out of the speakers, with Team USA's star-studded opening pairing arriving almost 10 minutes early to soak up the atmosphere.

Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz were quickly joined by Hull and rookie Lottie Woad, with every pair's arrival greeted with smoke cannons, huge cheers and cleverly thought-out adaptations of chants heard in other sports.

Image: Nelly Korda filmed the atmosphere around the tee ahead of beginning her match on Friday morning

A big message of 'quiet please' appeared on the big screens ahead of the opening tee shots, with a Corpuz-inspired adaptation of the Beatles classic 'Hey Jude' quickly cut for respectful silence as players hit their drives.

The party at the tee continued long after Woad rolled in the opening birdie of the event on the first green, with Team USA vice-captain Paula Creamer - wearing her cowboy hat - and fan favourite Megan Khang among those showcasing their dance moves.

"Ohhhh, Leona Maguire" was sung loudly to the tune of Kings of Leon's 'Sex on Fire', while Desmond Decker's 'Israelites' was adapted to fit in Esther Henseleit's name.

Remember the "Europe's on fire, USA is terrified" song chanted regularly during last year's Ryder Cup win at Bethpage Black? A Maguire twist was heard to recognise the Irishwoman with one of the best winning percentages in Solheim Cup history.

Dancing along to every song, arm in arm with the debutants during 'It's Raining Men' and when the DJ played a Vengaboys track, the Solheim stalwart seemed to never have anything but a huge grin on her face.

The positive vibes spread throughout the European team, with Maja Stark and Linn Grant running out to the crowd and swaying their hips to ABBA's karaoke classic 'Dancing Queen' as they awaited their match to get going.

"These people absolutely make it for the players," said Dame Laura Davies, a 12-time Solheim Cup player, said about the crowd. "Without these brilliant fans, it's just not the same."

"Maja Stark, doo-doo, doo-doo, doo-doo" - to the theme of Baby Shark - is an earworm nobody needs but works well with the Swede's name, with Stark and Linn Grant buoyed by the crowds to earn Team Europe's first point of the contest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Linn Grant and Maja Stark won Europe's first point of the Solheim Cup after beating Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan

The weather turning from early sunshine to persistent light rain didn't dampen the spirits of those following the action, with strong galleries lining the fairways to watch a tight opening session that left the teams tied at two apiece.

"We had incredible support out here," Maguire said after her win. "They were really spurring us on, especially when that weather got bad and miserable. It was that extra little bit we needed to grind it out."

The noise appeared to reach even higher levels during the afternoon session, where former major winner Karen Stupples described the crowds as 'insane'. If the quality of golf on the course matches the atmosphere being created off it, the 20th edition of the Solheim Cup could be one of the most memorable yet.

Sports.title: Sky Sports agrees three-year US Open extension
Sports.content:
Sky has agreed a three-year extension to its US Open deal, ensuring Sky Sports and NOW remains the exclusive home of the tournament in the UK and Ireland until the end of 2030.

As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

Sports.title: Russell tops first practice in Madrid as Hamilton frustrates other drivers
Sports.content:
George Russell was fastest from Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli in the first practice session at the new Madring circuit in Madrid.

Russell is looking to hit back after losing out to championship leader Antonelli last Sunday at Monza and started the Spanish Grand Prix weekend perfectly as he outpaced Antonelli by 0.286s.

But Ferrari were quick early on and were only half a second off the best times on the medium tyres, compared to the Mercedes on the softs.

Charles Leclerc, who is fit enough to race despite suffering from blurred vision in the aftermath of his huge Monza crash, eventually improved on the softs to third but Lewis Hamilton's best time remained on the mediums.

Hamilton was called out by at least four drivers for impeding across the practice hour as the tight confines of the Madring meant traffic was an issue.

Arvid Lindblad first called Hamilton and Antonelli "stupid" for blocking the track at the high-speed banked Turn 12 before Leclerc, Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Williams' Carlos Sainz all had to abandon flying laps due to the seven-time world champion not being aware of them coming.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Hamilton push the limits around the Madring Circuit at the Spanish Grand Prix

Sainz said on the radio of his incident: "Lewis letting by in the middle of Turn 12. It's always the same, it's so dangerous!

"Like it takes zero effort to be two metres more left. Zero effort!"

There were concerns about plenty of disruption in practice after 19 red flags were required in a two-day Formula 3 test last month, but all 22 F1 drivers kept it out of the barriers.

Track evolution was high throughout the session but it already looks like Mercedes and Ferrari are going to contend for top spot this weekend.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player F2 driver walks away after car goes up in flames!

"I'm really impressed with the way they approached this brand new circuit," said Sky Sports F1's Anthony Davidson.

"They made it look easy really - which they often do."

Red Bull's Max Verstappen was fifth ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris, while rookie Lindblad impressed in seventh for Racing Bulls.

Audi had strong pace with Nico Hulkenberg in ninth and Gabriel Bortoleto in 11th with Red Bull's Lawson in 10th.
