Sports.title: Man Utd's £1bn rebuild faces toughest test
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick transformed Manchester United's fortunes after his appointment in January, steering the side from seventh to third and clinching their return to the Champions League.

But Sunday's Manchester derby, only three days after their 4-0 win over Sabah, is the first test of how they will handle their busier schedule this season. Do they have the squad to manage the extra workload? And has their rebuild neglected one key area?

From 40 games to 60?

With no European football and early exits from the Carabao Cup and FA Cup against Grimsby Town and Brighton respectively, Manchester United only played 40 games in all competitions last term.

It was the joint-fewest of any Premier League side and the club's lowest total for a single season since the 1913/14 campaign.

The light schedule allowed Carrick to keep key players fresh while Manchester United's rivals were having to rotate. In the period between his appointment and the conclusion of the Premier League season, only five sides made fewer line-up changes than United.

That level of consistency in terms of selection is unlikely to be possible this season, with Thursday's game against Sabah the first of eight guaranteed Champions League fixtures. Manchester United could play as many as 67 games across all competitions.

Carrick has talked up the positives of a more demanding schedule.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Man Utd's draw with Everton

"It's less training once the season gets going, but a lot more involvement for the players," he said during pre-season. Carrick also made the point that the majority of his players are more accustomed to playing in Europe than not.

But the return to continental competition is still a test of their squad. The last time Manchester United juggled European commitments, in 2024/25, they finished 15th.

£1bn spent but squad still lacking

They should be well-equipped to cope with the extra workload.

Manchester United spent a middling £163m on new signings during the summer transfer window but they have invested more than £1bn in total since 2022 and have the highest net spend of any Premier League club in that timeframe, at £769.5m.

But there has been a lack of balance in their spending.

This summer, it was focused almost entirely on their midfield, with Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans the headline additions. A year ago, most of the money went on their attack as they signed Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

Their defence has so far been neglected.

Only 19 per cent of the £1bn spent since 2022 has gone on defenders. It is the third-lowest percentage of Premier League clubs in the same period, above only Liverpool and Everton, and falls way short of the 42 per cent spent on their forwards.

The result is the squad, although stronger in some areas, still lacks quality and depth in others. Manchester United's forwards are rated as the third-most valuable of the Premier League's big six but their midfielders and defenders are the least valuable.

And there are still question marks even in attack, where they have an abundance of supporting forwards including Mbeumo, Cunha and Amad Diallo, but only one out-and-out striker in Sesko.

They also lack a playmaking alternative to Bruno Fernandes.

Have Man Utd gone stale?

Despite spending upwards of £1bn over the last four years, Manchester United's team shows little turnover.

Amazingly, their back four for Sunday's 2-2 draw against Everton, made up of Luke Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot, was the same as in Erik Ten Hag's first game in May 2022.

Marcus Rashford's return to the fold, to the left of Fernandes, means six starters were the same in total, adding to the sense of a side that has gone stale, despite the club's huge spending.

Their retention rate of 54.5 per cent, from the first game of the 2022/23 season to the latest game of the new campaign, is by far the highest of any club, with Arsenal next on 36.4 per cent having retained Gabriel, Ben White, Martin Odegaard and Bukayo Saka.

Continuity can of course be positive. But while Gabriel, White, Odegaard and Saka have all played crucial roles in turning Arsenal into Premier League champions, many of Manchester United's retained starters are better known for underperformance.

The issue for Carrick, as he prepares to manage a far busier Manchester United schedule, is that his other options, particularly in defence, do not inspire much confidence either.

It all adds up to make his task tougher than last season.

Only two wins were secured by the underdog according to bookmakers, and one of those was Europa League champions Aston Villa beating Club Brugge. Hardly an upset when you compare their finances. Ghana will ​always be ‌a part ​of me.” His younger brother, Nico Williams, was part of the Spain side that won this year’s World Cup. Share

So, that’s where we’re at. It doesn’t mean that we can’t and we won’t. It means we still hope, we believe, and we expect that we can be and we should be, but I understand the bigger picture.” Share

He understands the game very well and has the experience which is quite good for our young team. I am very happy to have him in our team. I hope this level of performance and if he can improve it then even better.” Alexis Mac Allister ‘very sad’ Liverpool have not offered him a new contract Read more Share

2h ago 07.53 EDT Manchester United take action against ticket touts Manchester United believe they have disrupted organised ticketing networks having removed 685 season tickets as part of a contentious ticket touting investigation. The club’s heavy-handed summer crackdown resulted in widespread condemnations from fans and supporter groups after many innocent people faced the threat of sanction. The 1958 this week called for fans to “stand united” against the “season ticket ban fiasco” in a protest ahead of Sunday’s derby against Manchester City as a “line has been crossed”. United released an outcome update on their investigation ahead of this weekend’s action, revealing that 685 accounts have been subject to a ban while 464 supporters received a reduced sanction or final warning. A club statement read: “Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts. “These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United. Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list.” United say the investigation identified 1,617 accounts that required further review due to what it calls “unusual activity”. Of those stripped of season tickets, 113 failed to respond to requests for further information, 73 did not appeal and 499 received bans upheld by an independent appeals panel. (Press Association) Share Updated at 08.03 EDT

Physically, he’s in a really good place. I think he moves with confidence and technically we know he is very good. He is understanding better what we need from the number nine position.” Share

Sometimes it happens. I don’t have any doubt that United will be ready. It is a matter of adapting. It happened last season with us, this season with them, next season it will happen to someone else.” Share

It’s normal when Elliot said that,” said Maresca. “If you go back it’s a different picture, but for me the reason he said that is because when he grew up Manchester City was dominant.” Maresca backs Elliot Anderson over ‘kings of Manchester’ before derby clash Read more Share

3h ago 07.02 EDT Panic at Fulham? Not yet, though some distress flares. Brazilian winger Kevin, an unused substitute against Crystal Palace, added a cryptic message on his Instagram story with the caption ‘no speak, no hear, no see’. Alex Iwobi and Emile Smith Rowe have, meanwhile, both cleared their own Instagram posts of football-related content, with some fans interpreting it as growing signs of disharmony within the Fulham camp. Alvaro Arbeloa moved to calm waters today: “You can learn more about a group after a defeat than after a win, and I saw them work during the week with a very positive attitude, all of them,” the Fulham boss said at a press conference. “For sure when you are a player and you are not playing, you can’t be happy. It is what I expect from the players that are not playing. I want that they should need to show me that they are not happy during the training session. For me, this is the most important thing. “Obviously, when you are not winning games and you are not helping your team, I think you have more desire to play games and to help their team-mates. But all of them, they have been working so hard and I have a very, very good group with a very good attitude.” Fulham have lost all three league matches this season. Share Updated at 08.15 EDT

3h ago 06.56 EDT Time for another handover. John Brewin will be your news conduit for the next wee while. Catch you’se later. Share

3h ago 06.51 EDT Hull fined over offensive chanting. Anecdotally, you do detect a slight uptick in unpleasant chants from the tiresome edgelord element among clubs’ fanbases and Hull have copped a fine for the homophobic antics of some herberts in their support after last season’s Cup tie against Chelsea, as Reuters reports: Hull City have been fined £30,000 ($40,512) by the Football ⁠Association over discriminatory chanting during their FA Cup defeat by ⁠Chelsea in ⁠February, ​the governing body said on Friday. An independent regulatory commission also ⁠imposed an action plan on the club after it failed to prevent ⁠offensive chanting despite warnings over the public ​address system. “It was ‌alleged that ‌the club failed to ensure its spectators ‌and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters) do not use words or behave in an improper, offensive, abusive, indecent or insulting way with a reference – whether ‌express or implied – to sexual orientation,” read the statement. Offensive chanting was heard ​in sections of the home crowd during the first half of last season’s game, prompting an announcement over the PA ⁠system urging supporters to stop and reminding ​them ​that CCTV was in ​operation. A second announcement was made ​in the ‌second half ​confirming ​action had been taken, including arrests made. Hull City have admitted the charges. Share

3h ago 06.32 EDT There’s a lot of noise about Manchester United’s 15-year-old forward JJ Gabriel, and the volume was ramped up last night when he scored a hat-trick for the U19s in their 5-0 win against Sabah in the Uefa Youth League. Gabriel has already trained with Michael Carrick’s first team and his coach Adam Lawrence sung his praises again after Thursday’s showing, reports PA. “JJ is surrounded by people that really, really believe in him from the top of the club right the way through,” Lawrence said. “He’s been at the club for so long. He’s got real good relationships with the players, with the staff, so I think over the course of time obviously that helps as well. “At the moment, just in terms of his game, his games programme, his training programme, it’s about making sure that he’s getting the right exposure across different levels. We’re obviously not perfect but it’s definitely something we put a lot of thought into, so it’s good to see him enjoying his football in a good place.” “The first thing is that it’s my job is not to ruin him. When you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads, you obviously don’t want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. “What you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments. It can’t always be free and off the cuff, in terms of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he’s working on and the pressing that he’s thinking about. “But in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other team-mates at the top end of the pitch, he’s just in a real good space.” Share

4h ago 06.25 EDT Nico O’Reilly is set to return to the Manchester City side for Sunday’s derby at Manchester United. The England left-back has missed the last two games after pulling up with a back problem in the warm-up prior to last weekend’s Premier League victory over Coventry. Winger Jeremy Doku remains on the sidelines with the calf problem he sustained in the Community Shield but City have no other fitness concerns for the trip to Old Trafford. The manager, Enzo Maresca, said: “Nico is 100 per cent available but Jeremy, I think he needs some more days.” PA Share

4h ago 06.19 EDT Ed Aarons Mikel is being intense again … double quotation mark Mikel Arteta has revealed that he likes to set players challenges, such as delaying their meals before matches and making the dressing room hotter, to ensure they are fully prepared for any eventuality. Arsenal’s flight to Italy for their Champions League opener against Napoli this week was delayed for more than five hours, with Arteta forced to cancel his pre-match press conference after the squad arrived in Naples just before 10pm local time. The disruption proved no handicap as they made it 13 successive league-stage victories in Europe, thanks to Martin Ødegaard’s second-half winner. Arteta has a reputation for his innovative methods having previously employed pickpockets during pre-season training camps and preparing for a trip to Anfield by pumping crowd noises through a speaker. The Arsenal manager has now explained how his players have been trained to expect things to go wrong. “I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season,” he said. “So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking. “So, when that happens, adapt to it. ‘Okay, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them?’ Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but certainly don’t complain and then use it as an excuse because that’s not helpful at all.” Asked what other methods he has employed, Arteta added: “Just delay the meals, delay the transport, take a different route. We have done many things: make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kind of things. Because we are going to have to adapt to different contexts and we will try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is that element of stress or surprise on matchday, it’s important [to be prepared].” ‘Delay the meals’: Mikel Arteta reveals latest maverick Arsenal methods Read more Share

4h ago 06.14 EDT João Pedro named Premier League player of the month Morning everyone. Off to a game this weekend? What are your hopes and expectations? I always aim low in the vague hope of being pleasantly surprised. Anyway, the season’s first monthly awards are in, and João Pedro has been named the Premier League’s player of the month for August after registering two goals and two assists in Xabi Alonso’s side’s swashbuckling start to the season. He’s the first Chelsea player to win the award since Cole Palmer in September 2024, fact fans. The EFL’s monthly trinkets are in too, with Southampton’s Cyle Larin named Championship player of the month, while Jamal Lowe of Sheffield Wednesday and York’s Harry Boyes taking the League One and League Two awards respectively. The manager awards in the EFL went to Vítor Matos of Swansea (Championship), Huddersfield’s Martin Drury (League One) and Dean Brennan of Barnet (League Two). Share

4h ago 06.02 EDT Hull's Thomas 'unharmed' in car accident Thanks Tom. Hull City have confirmed that their winger Sorba Thomas was unhurt following a car accident this morning. After dramatic images were posted on social media, Hull issued a statement saying the Wales winger walked away unscathed. double quotation mark Hull City is relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground. The club is aware of images of Sorba’s car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed. Share

4h ago 05.59 EDT I’m grabbing a break from the blog, to see you through the next couple of hours is Tom Davies. Share

4h ago 05.57 EDT Matthias Jaissle revealed that summer signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo is edging closer to starting for Newcastle. The 21-year-old forward arrived on Tyneside from Lille on deadline day and has featured as a substitute in Newcastle’s last two matches. Speaking ahead of Monday’s clash with Leeds, Jaissle said: “Yeah, he’s getting closer. I said that we need to be smart with his load management. Now he’s getting more and more minutes. “He has now almost a full training week to Leeds, that helps him a lot. I think it’s the first time now since he arrived, and then we can make the decision on Sunday, maybe even on Monday.” Press Association Share Updated at 06.12 EDT

4h ago 05.37 EDT Spanish World Cup-winner Juan Mata has confirmed he will be departing Australian side Melbourne Victory, but stopped short of calling time on his career. The former Manchester United and Chelsea ace has enjoyed a late-career resurgence and was voted the domestic A-League player of the year in 2025-26. But the 38-year-old has decided not to play on at the club as he mulls “the next steps in his career”. He will remain involved with the Australian side after taking an ownership stake. “I loved every minute and so greatly enjoyed everything that we achieved last season, falling back in love with football at such a special place, in an amazing city that it was a privilege to call home,” Mata said. “Now I am excited about our next chapters, believing together in the future of Australian football and inspiring the next generation of Melbourne Victory players and supporters.” AFP Share

4h ago 05.33 EDT Gianni Infantino has not responded to a request to appear before the US House judiciary committee or sent documents requested by one of its members more than a month past the deadline. The Democrat Jamie Raskin, the ranking minority member of the committee, wrote to the Fifa president on 26 July informing the Swiss he was launching an investigation into “a sustained campaign” by Fifa to curry favour with the US president, Donald Trump. His letter said seeking of favours extended to the dismissal of high-profile corruption cases, while also accusing Fifa of “gouging” American consumers with “exorbitant” World Cup ticket prices this summer. The Swiss was asked to respond to the letter by 9 August with the requested documents and to make contact with the committee to schedule an interview, but it is understood no response at all had been received as of Thursday. Because no subpoena was issued, there are no criminal consequences for ignoring Raskin’s request. Press Association Share Updated at 05.34 EDT

5h ago 05.27 EDT In totally normal Turkish football news… the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job. Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks. Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added. Full story: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay Read more Share

5h ago 05.02 EDT The French football federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election. View image in fullscreen Gianni Infantino was accused by the French federation’s president of behaving in a ‘unilateral and opaque fashion’. Photograph: Jarek Praszkiewicz/EPA The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash. French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support Read more Share Updated at 06.12 EDT

5h ago 04.46 EDT United were the only Premier League club in Champions League action last night but Englishman Harry Kane scored for the eighth game in a row in the competition as Bayern Munich beat Bodø/Glimt 5-0 at the Allianz Arena. Starting their Champions League journey were Cesc Fabregas’s Como, who beat RB Leipzig 4-1 Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia, while Lens scored twice in added time to reverse a 2-1 deficit and secure a 3-2 win. Our roundup of all of Thursday night’s European action is here. Share

5h ago 04.37 EDT David Hytner Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire. View image in fullscreen Benjamin Sesko celebrates after scoring Manchester United’s third goal before half-time. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City. Read David Hytner’s full report from Old Trafford: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return Read more Share Updated at 06.12 EDT

6h ago 04.22 EDT Hall agrees contract extension Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall has signed a new long-term contract with the club. Reports suggest the left-back, 22, has agreed a two-year extension to his original deal that would take his contract up to 2031. Hall has been the subject of interest from Manchester United, among others, but has now committed his immediate future to Newcastle. “It’s an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters,” he said. “I know how much it means to them. “To be able to bring joy to their faces, it’s a big thing for me. I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all. “One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United.” Allow Instagram content? Sports.title: Champions League review: Irish heroics, rejected resignations and Mourinho’s return
Sports.content:
A big week for

The league phase has been previewed as Barcelona’s first step toward reclaiming a crown last lifted in 2015, with disappointments aplenty since. Lionel Messi claiming just one Champions League title in the last decade of his time at Camp Nou is the starkest statistic. The player anointed as Messi’s successor, Lamine Yamal, is already a European and world champion for Spain, so this is the next frontier. A soggy Wednesday evening at Camp Nou saw Hansi Flick’s team show their attacking chops remain of the highest quality in a 5-1 defeat of Feyenoord. The club presidential regime of Joan Laporta continues to pull levers to confound financial experts, with Gabriel Jesus, one of the summer’s arrivals, scoring his first Barca goal. Yamal got on the scoresheet via a scruffy free-kick after Raphinha had reminded there are further dimensions to that all-star attack, his first goal of his pair two sending Feyenoord defenders skidding.

Until Troy Parrott headed to Seville this summer, the chances of Real Betis v Lille being a leading attraction to the Irish diaspora were minimal. But now the team in green and white have become an Irish obsession. The goalscorer in their World Cup playoff win in Hungary last year is approaching national hero status. Opting for Andalusia instead of leading West Ham in the Championship confirmed him as a player with broad horizons; the former Tottenham trainee is hitting the heights in La Liga. Having scored the winner against Real Madrid last weekend, throwing back to José Mourinho his rejection when a Spurs teenager, he delivered again in northern France. His dragged, left-footed finish grabbed a 3-2 lead Betis successfully held. “I don’t think I’ll ever have a better night in my whole life,” Parrott said of his glory night in Budapest. If that still holds true, his Friday and Tuesday will have gone close to emulating it.

Weird scenes after Fenerbahce’s 1-1 draw with Roma when Ismail Kartal, the Turkish club’s veteran coach, resigned post-match “to clear the way”. The drama was heightened when the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildirim, said he would not be accepting the resignation. “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue,” Yildirim said. “I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s it. We are a family.” The explanation given for such a sudden exit was Kartal’s annoyance at a bottle being lobbed in his direction. Watch this space.

Player of the week

Ballon D’Or season is upon us, and a leading nominee must be Bayern’s brilliant Michael Olise, who scored two goals against Bodø/Glimt. The Norwegians attempted to aggressively mark him but were left with twisted blood as his team scored five second-half goals. The Frenchman gave a typically dry post-match interview. Asked how it feels to score great goals, he said: “I don’t know … I just shoot and it goes in.”

Club in focus

Manchester United on Thursday faced a club formed in 2017, three years after Luke Shaw, who missed the game, was signed. Sabah, Azerbaijan’s champions last season, breaking the dominance of Qurban Qurbanov’s Qarabag, are coached by Valdas Dambrauskas, a former United soccer schools and Brentford youth coach who also worked as a pub cleaner and gardener in the UK. His journey from Lithuania to Manchester was funded by a win on Who Wants To Be A Millionaire, where he walked away from Vilnius’s equivalent of Regis Philbin with a sum commensurate with a year’s salary. The homecoming was not too happy as United were ready 4-0 winners, Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes in particular turning on the style. “He absolutely destroyed us,” Dambrauskas said of Fernandes. That did not bode well for Sabah’s matches ahead: Dortmund, Barcelona and Napoli travel to Azerbaijan, while a trip to Arsenal awaits.

View image in fullscreen Azerbaijani champions Sabah and their quizshow contestant coach had no answers for Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

They said it

“There’s a lot of criticism when a match is boring, but it was crazy today. . … It could easily have ended 7-6. Our midfield was weak, they made changes very early, and I didn’t have much to work with in the centre of the pitch. … I agree with Raul that the goals came as a result of their errors.” José Mourinho’s Real Madrid return is already under scrutiny, and before being interviewed on Movistar after a close-run 2-1 defeat of Inter, he had to listen to on-air criticism from Raúl González, a Madrileno legend. Those midfield comments appeared directed at Trent Alexander-Arnold, who played as one of the trio on a night where fans at the Santiago Bernabéu made clear that better is expected.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Looking ahead

The other side of an elongated international break, the wait will be long – more than a month – for the second round of matches. Holders Paris Saint-Germain, looking for their third straight title, travelling to Manchester City is the grand-slam fixture. Enzo Maresca has made a decent fist of succeeding Pep Guardiola, with four wins in four. Erling Haaland’s pair of goals at Porto took him to 167, third on his club’s all-time scorers’ list, 10 behind Eric Brook, who played his last game during the second world war.

Mourinho, should he remain in charge at Real Madrid, will return to Roma while Manchester United travel to Atlético Madrid, who knocked out United in the last 16 in 2021-22, their only previous meeting in the competition.

Sports.title: Chelsea hand Pedro Neto new deal in wake of his rejecting Manchester City
Sports.content:
Chelsea have rewarded Pedro Neto’s strong start to the season and commitment to the club by handing the winger a new contract. The Portugal international had summer interest from several Premier League clubs including Manchester City, but indicated a desire to stay and play for Xabi Alonso. He has signed a five-year deal with the option of an extra year and is to receive a pay rise.

Alonso has used Neto as an attacking wingback and the 26-year-old has scored twice in five appearances. Neto, who has registered 40 goal involvements since joining from Wolves for £54m in 2024, follows other leading players at Chelsea in signing new deals. João Pedro, Reece James and Moisés Caicedo have received improved terms this year, and Cole Palmer signed a new deal in 2024 and committed his future to the club in an interview with the Guardian last season.

Chelsea’s owners have a strategy of giving lengthy incentivised contracts. However, the club have demonstrated that being on those multi-year deals will not stop players from receiving pay increases as reward for good performances. Further contract renewals are expected to be announced soon.

Neto’s determination to stay contrasted with the stance of Enzo Fernández, who was sold to City for £125m during the closing hours of the transfer window.

He was not handed a new contract after initial discussions were held. The Argentina midfielder raised questions over his future in March, criticising January’s departure of Enzo Maresca as head coach and sparking talk of a move to Real Madrid by expressing a desire to live in the Spanish capital. Chelsea responded by banning Fernández for two games.

Madrid downplayed their interest in Fernández but the 25-year-old continued to push for a new challenge. City, who appointed Maresca as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, emerged as Fernández’s strongest suitors. Chelsea were prepared to hold on to him if their valuation were not met but concluded that selling was the right long-term move. There was disappointment that one of the team’s senior players did not show better leadership when Chelsea were struggling. They missed out on European qualification after finishing 10th.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca and Enzo Fernandez during their time at Chelsea. They have been reunited at Manchester City. Photograph: Mark Pain/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

Chelsea sacked Liam Rosenior in April and announced Alonso’s appointment in mid-May. They were willing to reintegrate Fernández but he is understood to have submitted a written transfer request. It is understood he also informed Chelsea he had been in contact with a former coach, believed to be Maresca, at the end of last season and during the transfer window.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The Stamford Bridge hierarchy concluded that Fernández’s relationship with his teammates was broken after his public comments. Fernández’s representatives have been approached for comment.

Sources have dismissed the idea that Chelsea were bullied into selling Fernández. Neto’s renewal is viewed as the latest evidence that key players have bought into the project and will be rewarded.

Sports.title: Olid’s United on back foot due to late business and unforgiving WSL start
Sports.content:
It was tough watching Manchester United’s players labour ineffectively against the hungry and aggressive press of London City Lionesses in the Women’s Super League’s opening match. Simi Awujo’s late consolation goal did little to ease the mounting concern for a side that have several teams nipping at their heels.

Don’t panic; that has to be United’s message. To an extent, it is very early to be writing the team’s obituary. The new head coach, Eva Olid, had only three weeks to try to implement her ideas about the way the team should play before that match in Bromley on Friday 4 September. That is not long enough for her to peel away Marc Skinner’s imprint on the team.

The forward Monica Jusu Bah did not arrive from the Swedish side Häcken until 28 August and Rebeca Bernal signed from Washington Spirit on 2 September. United’s late business, in regards to their managerial change and transfer activity, has put the team and coaching staff on the back foot, playing catch-up with clubs who got most of their business done early in the window, the better to capitalise on the opportunity for a full pre-season presented by the lack of a major international tournament.

The problem is the spotlight is harsh on the red side of Manchester. The minority owner Jim Ratcliffe’s dismissive comments relating to the women’s team and the lack of serious investment in the squad provide reasons to be somewhat forgiving of the head coach and her charges, their struggles an indictment of a club that seemingly do not fully care.

The focus is said to be on a sustainable investment model recruitment-wise and on developing younger players. In isolation they are admirable goals, but in the context of investment gathering pace at other WSL teams and the relative pocket change required at a club of United’s stature to have a transformatory effect on the women’s side, these goals become shackles.

There is some irony in Olid leaving Hearts and coming to United. She arrived in Scotland to take charge of an amateur team that had avoided relegation only owing to the expansion of the top division and within five years had taken them to professionalism and a Scottish Women’s Premier League title. She felt the level of investment then needed to make Hearts competitive in Europe was lacking and it was announced that she would depart at the end of the season. The WSL and its teams are miles ahead, developmentally, of the SWPL and its sides but Olid has landed at a club that have repeatedly failed to invest substantially enough to make them league or European title challengers.

Olid told the Catalan newspaper Ara that she would have stayed at Hearts “if my project continued”. She said: “I wanted to coach in Europe, but it was a preliminary round and perhaps we would be there for a week and get eliminated. I don’t want to go backwards, I preferred to leave after winning everything because otherwise I would feel frustrated.”

View image in fullscreen Manchester United only lost 2-1 at London City Lionesses last Friday but were outclassed throughout the game. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Frustration was the name of the game at United under Skinner. The former head coach was frustrated with what he regarded as a lack of support in transfer windows and fans grew increasingly frustrated with a lack of sustained progress. United would take a step forward, such as winning the FA Cup in 2024 or reaching the Champions League quarter-finals last season, then fail to push on.

Patience is thin and Olid’s task has been made a lot harder by seven departures and only four additions to what many viewed as an already light squad. Olid has said she has had assurances that United will be active in the winter window. “We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play and game model,” she said in her first press conference.

However, United have 12 WSL games before January, plus cup games, and with Chelsea visiting on Sunday and a trip to Arsenal next Saturday, they have an extremely unforgiving start.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Olid deserves time and patience. She is well respected and comes with a wealth of experience in her native Spain across boys’ academy football and women’s football and spent time at Houston Dynamo in the US.

Alongside battling critics unimpressed with the state of the team in their opening WSL game or questioning her managerial pedigree, she must contend with wave after wave of appalling sexist comments on social media that greet her every appearance. That surely will take a toll.

If Olid is able to weather the storm of frustration – which will grow if the team falter while players get used to her philosophy – and to force United to loosen the purse strings, they will be huge accomplishments.

Unfortunately, even success on the pitch is unlikely to end the online comments; it will probably just shift their tone. She deserves better in so many ways. The hope will be that she can build a connection with the playing group that enables them to punch above their weight until reinforcements potentially appear in January.

Their first opportunity to fend off the vultures is when they welcome Chelsea to Leigh and, with the Blues unconvincing in the final third against Aston Villa last Saturday, they can have a little hope.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Ton up for hard-working McBurnie

With 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high-octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and, given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. Barry Glendenning

Chelsea v Hull, Saturday 3pm (all times BST)

2 Arbeloa must trust process as Iraola once did

This might be an opportune moment for Álvaro Arbeloa to meet Andoni Iraola, though perhaps not his Liverpool team. With three defeats and seven goals conceded from his first three Premier League games as Fulham head coach, questions are already being asked over the former Liverpool defender’s ambitious approach. Just as they were when Iraola failed to win any of his first nine league games in charge of Bournemouth. Trust yourself and the process, might be the Liverpool head coach’s advice if asked. Fulham have been creative under Arbeloa but are easily exposed defensively. Liverpool, starting to click in attack under their new head coach, have the assets to exploit Fulham’s weaknesses and subject Arbeloa to an uncomfortable Anfield return. Iraola’s wide options could be reduced, however, with Bradley Barcola suffering cramp on Wednesday – his first start since France’s World Cup semi-final loss – and Cody Gakpo nursing a minor injury. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Fulham, Saturday 3pm

3 Doucouré eagerly waiting Palace return

Cheick Doucouré has had a rotten run of luck with injuries. Just when the Mali midfielder looked as if he was ready to make a first Crystal Palace appearance since January 2025 in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, he was taken ill. Pierre Sage revealed last week that Doucouré looked as if he had “given him one million dollars” when he was informed he would be part of the matchday squad at Fulham, where Palace got off the mark with a 3-2 victory. Sage has confirmed that the 26-year-old, who has been sidelined with two serious knee injuries but was once a transfer target for Liverpool, could be involved against Ipswich at Selhurst Park on Saturday. Whenever he does return it is sure to be a heartwarming moment. Ed Aarons

Crystal Palace v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Cheick Doucouré returned to the Crystal Palace squad for last weekend’s trip to Fulham. Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images

4 Cherries must end late lapses

The midfield battle between Brentford and Bournemouth will be crucial on Saturday, with Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré setting the tempo for Keith Andrews’ physical side. Brentford top the Premier League for aerial duels won (22.3 per 90 mins), interceptions (11.3 per 90), and fouls committed (16.3 per 90). “They defend well as a team, their high pressing is good,” said Bournemouth’s Marco Rose, who is hoping to guide his side to a first Premier League victory of the season. “Their transition, they have fast players. They have quality everywhere on the pitch, and every situation.” Rose’s answer for Brentford’s aggressiveness should be Alex Scott, who leads his team for interceptions and has drawn nine fouls so far this campaign – the fourth-highest tally in the league. Late drama could also be the deciding factor at the Vitality Stadium. Despite leading in all three of their opening league fixtures, Bournemouth have picked up just two points and four of their five goals conceded have arrived from the 84th minute onwards. History favours their opponents too, as the Cherries have failed to win any of their eight top-flight meetings with the Bees. Yara El-Shaboury

Bournemouth v Brentford, Saturday 3pm

5 Jackson ready to fill Watkins’ Villa boots

A summer of change at Aston Villa inevitably prompted plenty of noise but most of their new signings were long-standing targets, none more so than Nicolas Jackson. Unai Emery kickstarted Jackson’s career at Villarreal and, after reuniting at Villa, the Senegal striker scored his first goal at Club Brugge on Tuesday after his initial £47.5m move. Jackson has replaced Ollie Watkins, who proved a reliable source of goals across six straight top-flight seasons, and the early evidence has been encouraging. “I had a couple of fights with him when he was at Chelsea so when he first came in I thought: ‘What’s he going to be like?’ but he’s a brilliant guy,” said the Villa captain, John McGinn. “There’s a lot of expectation with the transfer fee but he’s going to be a huge player for us.” Ben Fisher

Aston Villa v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

6 Signs of early-season panic at Spurs

Only the most pessimistic home fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be gripped by anything resembling the kind of dread, anxiety and outright terror that accompanied Everton’s visit on the final day of last season, but the return of David Moyes’ side so early in the current campaign will still make for nervous viewing. With no goals and just one point on the board after three league games, fan faith in Roberto De Zerbi – and the hundreds of millions of pounds lavished upon new signings – has created a prevailing presumption that Tottenham will soon start firing on at least some, if not all, cylinders. In Everton, Spurs welcome a team whose record in this corner of north London is worse than any other top-flight side’s. Should they fail to beat a team who have taken just seven points from the past 51 available to them away at Tottenham, the sounds of early but outright mutiny are likely to be audible from the stands. BG

Tottenham v Everton, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Stadium of Light to give Guimarães hot reception

Old acquaintance will be renewed at the Stadium of Light on Saturday evening. While Sunderland’s captain and midfield anchor, Granit Xhaka, needs no introduction to his former north London public, the home centre-half Dan Ballard is a former Arsenal youth captain who joined the Gunners’ academy at the age of eight. Then there is Bruno Guimarães. Newcastle’s former captain can expect a hot reception as his new side aim to extend their season-opening run of five straight wins (including the Community Shield). “Arsenal are flying, they’re one of the best teams in Europe,” says Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager. “It will be challenging but I’m very excited to experience this situation again.” Thanks to goals from Ballard and Brian Brobbey, Le Bris choreographed a 2-2 Premier League draw against Mikel Arteta’s side on Wearside last November. “When you face a strong opponent you can become a bit shy but the most important thing is to be ourselves,” says Le Bris. “Arsenal are so adaptive they will find solutions, so we must be flexible.” Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Arsenal, Saturday 8pm

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães returns to the northeast as Arsenal visit Sunderland on Saturday night. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

8 Coventry adding points to performances?

One of three teams, along with Aston Villa and Tottenham, yet to score a top-flight goal this season, Coventry were extremely unfortunate not to break their duck at Manchester City last weekend. Their having narrowly avoided handing Frank Lampard’s side an early opener, it took a string of excellent saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City took three points at the death. “They played really well against Manchester City and created a lot of chances,” said Fabian Hürzeler, who takes his Brighton team to the CBS Arena on Sunday afternoon. Having been scathing in his criticism of his own side’s lack of energy and intensity in their woeful first-half performance against Leeds, the German will be aware that a similarly lethargic performance from his team is unlikely to go unpunished. Particularly away from home against a promoted team that may be firing blanks, but visibly grew in confidence with each passing minute of their defeat by one of the league’s best teams. BG

Coventry v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

9 Contrasting Manchester teams face off in derby

Manchester derby No 199 features a fascinating showdown between two young managers operating in the sport’s rarefied air: Michael Carrick, 45, who seeks to guide Manchester United to an 82nd victory in the fixture, and Enzo Maresca, 46, who aims for Manchester City’s 63rd. As the great Pep Guardiola’s successor, the visiting Italian can be delighted at his team’s perfect record from their four games under him since the Community Shield defeat. Carrick, though, should be disappointed at the return from an opening three matches as United’s permanent manager: a defeat at Hull and draw at Everton, with the 5-2 home win over Ipswich sandwiched between. United fans will protest beforehand about the club’s approach to eradicating ticket touting, and the occasion should be particularly spicy and vibrant. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pm

View image in fullscreen Manchester United supporters protested about the club’s ticket policies at Hull and will do so again before the Manchester derby. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Battle of the goalkeepers at Elland Road

Two teams unbeaten in the Premier League this season, two German managers in the dugouts and a Monday night goalkeeping beauty contest at Elland Road. While Daniel Farke welcomes his compatriot Matthias Jaissle to West Yorkshire for the first time, James Trafford – the £40m England keeper Newcastle tried to sign on three separate occasions – will be in goal for Leeds. The visitors eventually turned their attentions to the £26m Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who arrived on Tyneside from Braga in July. So far at least, Jaissle is delighted by the 24-year-old’s performances. “Lukas is an amazing signing,” said Jaissle. “Coming to the Premier League and dealing with the pressure is not easy and, as a keeper, that pressure is something else. I like Lukas a lot. He’s so calm but so mature as well. There’s not even a hint of nervousness. He gives the whole team confidence. That helps a lot.” LT

Sports.title: Maresca backs Anderson over ‘kings of Manchester’ dig before derby clash
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca has backed Elliot Anderson’s assessment that Manchester City are the “kings of Manchester” as he prepares for his first derby in charge of the club.

City travel to Old Trafford on Sunday seeking to continue their perfect start to life under Maresca and further prove Anderson’s point. The 23-year-old midfielder made his claim upon signing from Nottingham Forest for £116m in the summer and having witnessed from afar City win eight Premier League titles during the past 14 years, compared with United’s one.

“I think Manchester City was unbelievable what they achieved. It’s normal when Elliot said that,” said Maresca. “If you go back it’s a different picture, but for me the reason he said that is because when he grew up Manchester City was dominant.”

Michael Carrick refused to accept Anderson’s claim when speaking after United’s Champions League win against Sabah on Thursday night. “I’m definitely not using that phrase at all,” he said. “We’re humble enough and realistic enough to know where we’ve come from in recent history, and we need to and want to be better, and we want to be challenging more. So, that’s where we’re at. It doesn’t mean that we can’t and we won’t. It means we still hope, we believe, and we expect that we can be and we should be. But I understand the bigger picture.”

Carrick also suggested the short turnaround afforded to United from playing Sabah to facing City was “not ideal”, especially given City had a further two days to prepare for the fixture, having beaten Porto away on Tuesday. Pep Guardiola was often vocal on the subject of fixture scheduling but Maresca has taken it more in his stride and offered little sympathy to his opposite number. “To be honest, the club mentioned to me that it happened exactly the same last year when the club played Napoli and then after two days played Arsenal,” he said.

“Sometimes it happens in football. I don’t have any doubt that Man United are going to be ready for that. It just matters to adapt. I think that happens and you need to adapt. It happened last year with us, this season with them, next season it will happen with a different team.”

Maresca will welcome back Nico O’Reilly after the midfielder was a late withdrawal from the win over Coventry last week and missed the trip to Portugal with a back problem, but Jérémy Doku is not fit to return from a calf injury picked up in the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

Across his career as a player and coach, Maresca has been involved in some of the game’s biggest rivalries, enjoying the Manchester derby as part of Guardiola’s backroom staff. “I promise you the worst one is Olympiakos-Panathinaikos [in Athens]. That is very hot,” Maresca said. “I think they [derbies] are all special games for everyone. For the fans, first of all, for the club, for the players, for the coaching staff.”

Sports.title: ‘Delay the meals’: Mikel Arteta reveals latest maverick Arsenal methods
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has revealed that he likes to set players challenges, such as delaying their meals before matches and making the dressing room hotter, to ensure they are fully prepared for any eventuality.

Arsenal’s flight to Italy for their Champions League opener against Napoli this week was delayed for more than five hours, with Arteta forced to cancel his pre-match press conference after the squad arrived in Naples just before 10pm local time. The disruption proved no handicap as they made it 13 successive league-stage victories in Europe, thanks to Martin Ødegaard’s second-half winner.

Arteta has a reputation for his innovative methods having previously employed pickpockets during pre-season training camps and preparing for a trip to Anfield by pumping crowd noises through a speaker. The Arsenal manager has now explained how his players have been trained to expect things to go wrong. “I love those challenges. I try to create them in pre-season,” he said. “So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine as soon as the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic, and I don’t want the players, the staff as well, panicking.

“So, when that happens, adapt to it. ‘OK, we have another two or three hours on the plane, how can we use them?’ Play together, spend some time together, sleep, use it, but certainly don’t complain and then use it as an excuse because that’s not helpful at all.”

Asked what other methods he has employed, Arteta added: “Just delay the meals, delay the transport, take a different route. We have done many things: make the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less [massage] beds. Those kind of things. Because we are going to have to adapt to different contexts and we will try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions. But when there is that element of stress or surprise on matchday, it’s important [to be prepared].”

Arsenal travel to Sunderland on Saturday night looking to extend their 100% start to the new campaign after being held to a 2-2 draw at the Stadium of Light last year. Leandro Trossard scored Arsenal’s second goal before Brian Brobbey’s late equaliser and Arteta contrasted the Belgium forward’s reaction to leaving in the summer with that of Gabriel Jesus. “No one told me nothing,” said the Brazilian, who was made to train separately from the rest of Arsenal’s squad before moving to Barcelona. Trossard, meanwhile, was at the Emirates for last week’s win over Chelsea having joined Beskitas in July.

“Very surprised, to be fair, especially because with Gabriel I had an individual talk in the dressing room,” said Arteta. “And the words that we used for each other, it was all about gratitude. So, I don’t know. It’s OK. Sometimes I understand when you have to deliver bad news or news that people don’t expect. Those things are reactive. Somebody has to be the bad cop; if I have to be, I have to be.

“What is important is normally what happens three months later, six months later. When Trossard comes in, he’s in the dressing room with all of us, the atmosphere and the relation you have with all the players that they left, at some point their relationship has been really good. I hope that’s the same case.”

Sports.title: Pochettino’s ‘different’ vow to the US invites unwelcome speculation
Sports.content:
I hope, in this lifetime, you find someone who loves you the way Mauricio Pochettino loves Tottenham Hotspur. The grip Spurs have on his heart seems the stuff of a literary classic: his imperfect partner who called things off at the first sign of trouble must merely check in on him occasionally to rekindle hopes of a reunion.

Perhaps a bit extreme, but this week’s revelation – that he’d return to Tottenham even if they were relegated and chalking his absence up to imperfect timing, not the part about handing the club a decade-old title – has implicity laid out the terms of his return as United States manager. Others may always have interest in his services, and a certain North London suitor will never get the door slammed in their face outright.

“Now it’s a four-year contract, it’s different,” Pochettino said this week. “We can next season lose the Copa América or the Gold Cup, they’re not happy with us and they can sack us. Or we can say: ‘OK. It’s not in the way that we think.’ Four years is different. Maybe now if someone calls in the future, it’s a different, different type [of thing]. We are excited, we are thinking to spend four years to the next World Cup. But now it’s a long period.”

If you’re a Spurs fan, it warms the heart to revisit last decade’s glory days. If you’re a US fan, you’re quite sick of hearing so much about a team besides the one he’s managing. If you’ve been cursed to support both, this must be a very confusing time. And if you’re US Soccer, you know that you no longer have an ace in the hole to outflank any outside interest.

One can’t undersell the appeal of coaching a World Cup host team, with a direct path to Pot One and raucous support for every match. Already a familiar face to Americans who follow the sport, Pochettino became a genuine sensation in the broader sports landscape. Millions of Americans had parallel thoughts that he, clad handsomely in a $500 safari shirt, resembled Russell Crowe – perhaps tacitly revealing that millions of Americans have long undersold the appeal of Russell Crowe.

Compared to his previous post at Chelsea, the US job offered relative reprieve. Never before has Pochettino been such a prolific fixture on hours-long podcasts. The stop/start cadence of international management is appealing for the football men who have grown weary of the meticulous corporatization of the club game. In that sense, Pochettino is among esteemed company.

Two years after Jürgen Klopp left Liverpool citing mental exhaustion, he has refreshed his tracksuit collection with fresh duds from Die Mannschaft. In his opening press conference, he read aloud to the press his terms of service – and was celebrated for it. Carlo Ancelotti was in no rush to abandon Brazil after a middling tournament, despite real questions about the pool’s depth and quality in midfield. Even Pep Guardiola held talks with Italy immediately after his decade in Manchester.

What’s different about Pochettino from, say, Klopp is his perceived eagerness to return to the club grind. Even atop the Red Bull Football conglomerate, Klopp was quick to brush aside any insinuations about returning to management. Pochettino, by contrast, held talks with Milan about their coaching vacancy immediately before the 2026 World Cup.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There may be a simple answer. Each of Ancelotti, Guardiola, and Klopp – company with which Pochettino is regularly associated – has been the champion of England and Europe. Pochettino, at this stage, has not reached those summits.

Is aiming for a Copa América semi-final more enticing than restoring Tottenham to previous heights? What about reaching a World Cup quarter-final an ocean away from the tens of thousands who soundtracked the previous one? What can US Soccer offer that his caliber of clubs – Tottenham and beyond – can’t exceed?

While Pochettino and his charges have something resembling an excuse for their lack of execution against Belgium, the fact remains that the USMNT were once again eliminated in the last-16. Just like they were under Bob Bradley in 2010. And Jürgen Klinsmann in 2014. And Gregg Berhalter in 2022.

In theory, Pochettino will enter his second cycle in a position of strength having undertaken a thorough examination of the player pool. The fresh faces are no longer MLS journeymen or players in Europe’s lesser divisions. Instead, they’re promising prospects: 16-year-old wonderkid Cavan Sullivan, new Crystal Palace showman Zavier Gozo, highly anticipated La Masia netminder Diego Kochen.

If anything, working the up-and-comers into the established core and identifying sturdier central defenders to partner with Chris Richards should be an incredibly exciting project. The core is in great shape, with this summer’s headliners – Folarin Balogun, Alex Freeman, Richards, and Malik Tillman – all aged 30 or younger in the summer of 2030. There’s plenty of reason to think that the program is better positioned for a deep run at the next World Cup than the 2026.

Actualizing that potential will require a clear vision and a dedicated effort to raise this team’s standard throughout every window of the next four years. Batting eyelashes at past employers hardly projects that level of dedication. And so, for the next four years just like the past one, the biggest question surrounding the USMNT won’t be how far they can go in 2030. It’ll be whether Pochettino will still be the man leading them there.
