Sports.title: How nepo-baby Ben Shelton became US tennis' new superstar: Big-hitting American downed Carlos Alcaraz, is dating NBA legend Dennis Rodman's daughter and is now on the cusp of a $10MILLION brand deal after New York exploits
Sports.content:
If you had told Ben Shelton he would play the second US Open semi-final of his career tonight in July, he might not have believed you. The 23-year-old had endured a blink-and-you’ll-miss-it first-round exit at Wimbledon and he was frustrated.

‘It's been a weird season for me this year,’ Shelton admitted. He had three titles under his belt, but a string of early exits where it mattered - the majors and Masters. There were so many things that disappointed him in his game.

But two months is a long time in tennis. Shelton started August by defending his Canadian Open title, before taking his form to New York and beating Carlos Alcaraz in a late-night instant classic.

His meeting on Friday evening with fellow American Frances Tiafoe is not the first time he’s been at this stage. In 2023, he was a gregarious upstart one year into his career, with the unvarnished gifts, and ego, of a champion-in-waiting.

He had a controversial celebration: hanging up the phone on his opponents. He had hyped himself before the tournament saying he was looking to become someone players feared in the draw. And Shelton was, until Novak Djokovic hung up on him, winning in straight sets.

At 20 years old, Shelton had become box office. A tennis nepo-baby, Shelton is the son of former tour journeyman Bryan Shelton, but as a child, saw the family business as ‘boring’, preferring American football or basketball. It’s no stretch to imagine the left arm that provides his 146mph serve attached to an NFL quarterback. After he switched full focus to tennis at 13 however, Bryan now sits in his box as coach.

Add to family lore the draw of Shelton being one-half of one of America's sportiest power couples. Since sliding into his Instagram DMs in early 2025, USWNT star Trinity Rodman - daughter of NBA legend Dennis - is a frequent fixture on tour, with Shelton pitchside for her Washington Spirit matches when the ATP’s gruelling schedule allows.

Ben Shelton's courageous showing in his US Open quarter-final against Alcaraz has given him a shot at the final

The 23-year-old has reached this stage before in 2023 (left) - before Novak Djokovic hung up on him to win his 24th Grand Slam

Shelton is now frequently accompanied by his girlfriend Trinity Rodman - a blockbuster USA athlete in her own right

All this has brought Shelton attention, celebrity and riches - after three years wearing Roger Federer’s ON brand, he is reportedly set to ink a $10million deal with New Balance - but results? That’s where things get more complicated.

Shelton has been dogged by inconsistencies, particularly at the Grand Slams. In Paris, he has never made it past the fourth round, and Wimbledon’s 2025 quarter-final is an outlier amid early exits. Never mind that he has titles on both of the natural surfaces. When asked to perform on the biggest stages, his standout attributes can turn into fatal flaws.

‘That’s the challenge, working with a guy like Ben, who is very aggressive,’ his father said in July. ‘There are times when he crosses that line and sabotages himself, and doesn’t make it to the second or third round of the tournament.’

But the win against Alcaraz showed the soaring height of his ceiling. The biggest weapon is his serve. Keeping himself in top condition to deploy it leaves him covered in cupping marks. Shelton is devoted to the traditional Chinese medicine technique for recovery and would sooner skip tending to his arm than Samson would book in for a buzzcut.

Shelton is also a superior athlete, and proved he was able to match Alcaraz’s lightning-quick movement with his own work-rate, chasing down shots which should have been impossible, and getting them back over the net with flair.

If Shelton can play like he did against the Spaniard twice more, he could end America’s 23-year wait for a home men’s Grand Slam winner. But to do that, he has to pass another psychological test by defeating his close friend Tiafoe. Tiafoe is a three-time finalist and a fellow showman who saves his very best for his home Slam.

Like Shelton, Tiafoe saw out his own five-set comeback epic to reach the semi-finals, and having met twice before, their head-to-head at the tournament sits tantalisingly at one win apiece.

He has met US Open semi-final rival - and fellow American - Frances Tiafoe twice before at their home Grand Slam (pictured in 2023)

After beating Alcaraz, Rodman prompted Shelton to bring back his once-iconic celebration - his confidence has hit new heights at just the right time

The final series of their trilogy has added potency, their clash guaranteeing a Black US Open men’s finalist for the first time on Arthur Ashe since, well, Arthur Ashe in 1972. History is on the line.

But Shelton’s form has been cresting, and he will come into their contest buoyed up by his meeting with Alcaraz with lethal confidence.

At 3.34am on Wednesday morning, Shelton looked up to his player’s box. There, Rodman cheekily picked up the phone, like it was 2023 again. Shelton has learned a lot in three years. But he still answered.

Sports.title: Man United ban 685 accounts in ticket tout crackdown - as fans claim 'a line has been crossed' ahead of derby protest
Sports.content:
Man United ban 685 accounts in ticket tout crackdown - as fans claim 'a line has been crossed' ahead of derby protest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have revealed the outcome of the club’s clampdown on ticket touts ahead of a planned protest by fans before Sunday’s Old Trafford derby.

United confirmed that out of a total of 1,617 accounts identified as suspicious, 685 have been hit with a ban for breaching season-ticket rules.

Sources insist the club have broken up large-scale organised networks involved in touting based on the strongest data ever gathered.

However, United also acknowledge the frustration among fans over the crackdown that has led to Sunday’s protest before the game against Manchester City at Old Trafford.

Organisers The 1958 say ‘a line has been crossed’, accusing the club of issuing bans without providing clear evidence and targeting innocent fans.

United sources have denied that is the case and say a total of 468 cases were resolved without any further action. They insist that some examples shared on social media are untrue and don’t tell the full story.

Fans protested against the club on the opening game of the season against Hull

A club statement read: ‘Where satisfactory explanations were provided, restrictions were removed and no further action was taken. In many of those cases, the cause was sharing of account details and passwords, which is in breach of our terms and conditions.

‘We recognise that many supporters have shared account login details in circumstances they regarded as legitimate, and we did not anticipate the extent to which this was occurring. In those cases, where there was no additional evidence of misuse, no sanction was imposed.’

As a result of the investigation, United maintain that more tickets will now be available to genuine supporters rather than touts who they say were exploiting fans.

Out of the 685 accounts that have been banned, there were 499 cases in which fans lost an appeal, 73 cases where there was no appeal, and 113 where there was no response despite requests for information. A further 464 supporters received a reduced sanction or final warning.

The statement added: ‘Over the course of the summer, Manchester United undertook an operation to review accounts that showed irregular activity resembling ticket misuse. We committed to providing a further update once our investigation had concluded.

‘The club's guiding principle around ticketing is simple: to keep our fans safe and secure, to protect fair access to tickets for genuine Manchester United supporters and to tackle ticket touting, misuse and activity for financial gain.

‘Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts. These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

‘Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list. Refunds have been or will be issued to each of the season ticket holders who have been banned.

‘We want to allow any sanctioned ticket holder the opportunity to refer their case to the Independent Football Ombudsman. Therefore, we will wait until after the international break before reallocating season tickets. Any seats used on a match-by-match basis before then will be sold at season ticket prices, not matchday prices. The club is not profiting from this process.’

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton's mother recalls last hug with boxing champion three days before he took his own life a year ago as parents speak out for first time
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton's mother has recalled her last hug with him three days before he took his own life one year ago as his parents speak out for the first time.

Carol and Ray Hatton have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late after the boxing champion hanged himself on September 14 last year.

One year on from Ricky's death, aged 46, his mother has revealed the last time she embraced her son.

Just days before he took his own life, the boxing champion had been in an argument with his parents but the family were 'building bridges'.

Carol decided to make an unplanned visit to his gym in Hyde and gave him a 'real proper hug'.

She told ITV News: 'I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car. He asked if everything was okay.

'I said "yeah, everything's fine". I said I'd like to see a bit more of him.'

Ricky's mother said he told her he wanted to see his father Ray the next week. However Ricky died three days later.

Former world boxing champion Ricky Hatton died by suicide in September last year aged 46

Ray and Carol Hatton (pictured at their son's funeral) have urged people to tell their friends and family they love them before it's too late

Ricky had previously opened up about his struggle with drug and alcohol addiction and had become estranged from his parents before the reconciled

She added: 'I'm so glad (I got to see him) because nobody knows when it's the last time you're going to see somebody.'

Ray, the boxer's father, said: 'You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don't ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him.'

Ricky had become estranged from his parents for around a decade before he reached out to patch up their relationship several years before his death.

He had survived previous suicide attempts and struggled with drug and alcohol addiction.

Ricky fell out with his parents over money and despite the dispute he still allowed Carol and Ray to see his newborn daughter Millie.

However the boxer became upset when his girlfriend Jennifer was not invited to a Christmas Day party.

Months later he received letters from his parents' lawyers saying they wanted to see their granddaughter.

But he told Manchester Evening News in 2013 that he responded by saying: 'I replied to my parents, through solicitors, and said we did not want them to have contact with Millie.'

Carol Hatton wipes a tear from her eye while reading a statement at her home after Ricky's death

Ricky had survived previous suicide attempts before he died in September last year

'We have never stopped them seeing her, as far as I was concerned they had just not been ******.

'I know that sounds harsh and I am sure they see it differently, but it is how I feel.'

He added that the situation 'was a mess', describing the family feud as 'bitter and horrible', referring to back-and-forth letters between his and his parents' lawyers.

This culminated in his father attacking him in a car park fist fight.

Angry about 'all that stuff you've written about your mum in that solicitor's letter', Ray then punched his boxing champion son in the face before Ricky hit back and his father then drove off.

But Ricky's parents are still struggling to come to terms with his death and Carol said the couple 'have to move forward' but will continue 'remembering him and loving him'.

Carol and Ray have now called for a statue of Ricky to be erected in Manchester, saying it would be a 'fitting tribute' to their son who 'brought a lot of pride' to the city.

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury looks set for CARDIFF - at 2am: Welsh venue set to waive curfew to take boxing's biggest fight away from Wembley and New York
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Principality Stadium now looks set to be the unlikely winner of the venue war for boxing's biggest fight - by hosting Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury in the early hours of the morning.

The local authorities could today approve lifting the stadium's 10.30pm curfew to host the fight - stepping in after rows over holding it at Wembley Stadium or Madison Square Garden in New York.

Cardiff has history of hosting late-night boxing. Joe Calzaghe fought Mikkel Kessler at the Principality in 2007 at 2am. Fury and Joshua could fight at a similar time to satisfy broadcaster Netflix's huge audience in the United States.

Netflix had wanted the fight in New York to suit their prime timezones, while Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn pitched Wembley to host under the guise that Britain's biggest fight of the century should be hosted in the UK - and he has refused to budge unless contracts are rewritten with upgraded financial offerings.

Cardiff now appears to be the compromise. The Principality Stadium has an 80,000 capacity and a retractable roof - unlike Wembley - which could be useful in late November or December. A date of Saturday, November 28 has been mooted.

The Times report a press conference is tentatively scheduled for next week pending the approval.

Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could now be set to fight in Cardiff, Wales in November

Joshua and his camp wanted the fight in the UK - while broadcasters Netflix wanted a US host

Wembley looked an ideal venue for the fight but the strict 11pm curfew has been a sticking point, despite London mayor Sadiq Khan saying he wanted to ensure allowances were made to host the fight.

Boxing dealmaker Turki Al-Sheikh has been insistent on a start time of 2am.

Netflix have been running s for Fury-Joshua as recently as Thursday night, clearly confident an agreement will be struck.

The streaming giant has yet to sign off on Cardiff but American sportswriter Dan Rafael last night reported he had asked Netflix if they would approve, with a source telling him: 'I think they're OK.'

A spokesperson for the Welsh Rugby Union said: 'We'd be delighted to host this fight.

'We are very keen to attract more boxing to the stadium, which has a rich history in the sport, enhanced by its closable roof, unrivalled sight lines and unique city-centre location.'

Joe Calzaghe trains at the Principality Stadium before his 2am fight there in 2007

Joshua has fought in Cardiff twice previously, beating Carlos Takam and Joseph Parker in the Welsh capital in 2017 and 2018.

While Joshua has left Hearn to do the talking on his side of the deal, Fury has been publicly speaking and threatening that the heavyweight contest will be called off.

This week he suggested he will no longer be fighting Joshua in another social media rant as rows over the location and contract surrounding the fight continued.

'So it looks like AJ has s*** his pants yet again,' Fury said on social media on Sunday. 'After 11 years, he's finally s*** his pants yet again.'

Last week, Fury, who regularly takes to social media to express his views on potential opponents, was keen to make clear he feels Joshua is not motivated by a love of his country. Earlier this year Daily Mail Sport revealed Joshua had in fact quit the UK to move to Dubai – even as thousands tried to flee amid rising panic in the Middle East warzone.

And Fury, a tax exile to the Isle of Man himself, brought up a 2020 speech at a Black Lives Matter march, where Joshua read out a letter from his friend Reece Campbell to urge attendees to stop spending money with white-owned shops and businesses.

'Show them where it hurts', Joshua had said. 'Abstain from spending your money in their shops and economies, and invest in black-owned businesses.'

Fury re-posted the video of the speech, writing: 'This is the man who loves England, absolute s*** bag! Total piece of s*** bully with zero guts! Don't let them deceive you! & Living in Dubai.'

Provided Cardiff hits no further stumbling blocks, the Welsh capital may now offer the solution to get the fight on at last.

Sports.title: Darren Fletcher puts 'abusive' Man United autograph-hunters in their place: Coach shouts back after angry fans attacked players for not stopping when they wanted to meet their heroes
Sports.content:
See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United coach Darren Fletcher hit back at an 'abusive' fan after he did not sign an autograph following their Champions League win over Sabah.

Footage shared on social media showed Fletcher walking over to a section of Man United supporters, who had been waiting close to the team buses after their 4-0 win at Old Trafford on Thursday night.

Fletcher, who is currently the head coach of Man United's Under-18 side, specifically picked out one supporter having taken exception to their language.

Daily Mail Sport understands Fletcher had signed autographs for several fans but did not go all the way behind the bus where some supporters were waiting.

After one of those fans became abusive, Fletcher returned and shouted back at the supporter in response.

'Hey listen, it doesn't matter you can't speak like that,' Fletcher said, prompting cheers from other Man United supporters in attendance.

Darren Fletcher took aim at an 'abusive' autograph hunter after Man United's victory over Sabah in the Champions League

The fan had reportedly been angered after Fletcher had not walked around to sign an autograph, having done so for others

Fletcher then pointed at the fan and stated: 'You are the reason people don't sign, you are the reason people don't sign.'

His intervention led to fans chanting 'legend, legend' in support of Fletcher as he walked away.

Fletcher, now 42, has been head coach of Man United's Under-18 side since July last year.

He briefly stepped up to have a two-game spell as interim manager last January after Ruben Amorim's sacking, before Michael Carrick took charge.

During his career, Fletcher had made 342 appearances and scored 24 goals for Man United.

He won five Premier League titles, the Champions League and FA Cup during his playing career at Old Trafford.

Fletcher's former team-mate Patrice Evra previously claimed Sir Alex Ferguson had once torn into his players after failing to sign autographs when on a pre-season tour.

While players have been criticised in recent years for refusing to stop to sign autographs, Daily Mail Sport has previously revealed that Man United have grown increasingly frustrated with professional autograph hunters.

Concerns have previously been raised that players have been harangued as part of ‘industrial-scale autograph harvesting’ at Old Trafford, with signed memorabilia then being sold.

Manchester United had earned a 4-0 win over Sabah in the Champions League on Thursday

Man United had recorded a comfortable 4-0 win on Thursday night on their return to the Champions League.

First half goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko had seen the Red Devils storm into a 3-0 lead against tournament newcomers Sabah.

Lisandro Martinez added a fourth in the second half against their opponents from Azerbaijan.

The Red Devils will now turn their attentions to Sunday's Manchester derby.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta reveals his new bonkers management technique: SABOTAGING his own team! Arsenal boss 'delayed transport, ramped up dressing room thermostats and removed beds' to 'challenge' his players
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta reveals his new bonkers management technique: SABOTAGING his own team! Arsenal boss 'delayed transport, ramped up dressing room thermostats and removed beds' to 'challenge' his players

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Mikel Arteta has revealed he deliberately delayed transport and meals, removed massage beds and made the changing rooms hotter to challenge his players during pre-season.

The Arsenal boss has previously turned heads before with his training-ground methods as he bids to keep the champions one step ahead of the pursuing pack.

Arteta was famed for his use of speakers in training (not just blasting 'You'll Never Walk Alone' before a 4-0 defeat at Anfield in 2021), bringing in team dog Win and once hired 'pickpockets' to keep his team alert at all times.

The Arsenal boss revealed his latest attempts to challenge his players and staff after the Gunners were caught up in the air traffic control chaos this week, which led to thousands of flights being delayed and cancelled.

Their trip to Naples for their Champions League opener was among those affected on Tuesday, but the Gunners eventually travelled and secured a 1-0 victory over Napoli.

'I love those challenges, I try to create them in pre-season. So when they happen, we already experience them and we already know,' Arteta said.

Mikel Arteta has revealed he created challenges for his Arsenal team during their pre-season

Arteta admitted he delayed Arsenal's transport and meal times, as well as removing massage beds and made changing rooms hotter to test his players

Arteta made the revelation after Arsenal beat Napoli in the Champions League in midweek, despite their travel plans being disrupted in the build-up

'So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else. Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there's so much traffic and I don't want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking.

'When that happens, adapt to it. Okay, we have another two or three hours on the plane. How can we use them, play together, spend some time together, sleep?

'Use it, but certainly don't complain and then use it as an excuse because that's not helpful at all.'

Arteta expanded on how he challenged his players and staff this pre-season, adding: 'Just delaying the meals, delaying the transport, taking a different route.'

'We've done many things, made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds.

'Those kind of things, I think, in my opinion, because we're going to have to adapt to different contexts, and we'll try to anticipate it and create the best possible conditions.

'But when there is not that element of surprise or stress on matchday, I think it's important.’

Arteta's unusual methods have been dismissed by some in the past but the Gunners boss ultimately succeeded in delivering the club's first title in 22 years last season.

Arsenal are currently joint top of the Premier League heading into an away trip to Sunderland on Saturday night.

Only Arsenal and Man City boast a 100 per cent winning record from their opening three league matches of the campaign.

Sports.title: How Aaron Ramsdale fell to become FOURTH-CHOICE in the Championship: Insiders speak out on ex-Arsenal keeper - now playing in front of just 246 fans after transfers worth £80m
Sports.content:
When Aaron Ramsdale was in the early days of his career, he would often turn to the fans behind him and tell them a joke.

Sometimes a cracker, sometimes not. He was in the lower leagues back then so the supporters were so close to the goal he could almost feel the breath from their laughter. For Ramsdale, it was his way of coping with the pressure of being in the eye of the storm.

Those exchanges with the crowd became a release valve that remained with him ever since. He slid on his knees in front of the Manchester United fans. He joined in with Leicester supporters' chants of 'You're s***, ahhh' after his goal-kicks. He kissed the Arsenal badge in front of Spurs fans after the north London derby, though one of them climbed the hoardings and kicked him in the back.

It was his way, too, of staying focused. Three years ago, he revealed to an astonished Ian Wright how he was unable to keep his mind dialled in from the first whistle to the last. 'To concentrate on a game of football for 90 minutes, I'm finished, I can't do it,' said Ramsdale.

'That's why I get involved with the fans. I sing along with the songs. Someone's giving me abuse, I'll turn around and give it back. I've had my two, three minutes of madness in my head, straight back to the football and I've got 10-15 minutes of pure concentration again.'

Whatever your view of the methodology, it's one that has, until now, kept him in the eye of ever greater, more prominent storms. Five England caps. On the bench at Euro 2020, Euro 2024 and the World Cup in 2022. Arsenal's No 1. Named in the PFA team of the year in 2023 when the Gunners finished second under Mikel Arteta for the first time.

Aaron Ramsdale is effectively fourth-choice goalkeeper at Southampton in the Championship

Ramsdale was one Arsenal's No 1 and named as the Premier League's finest goalkeeper

Back in March, while on loan at Newcastle, he stood between the posts in front of nearly 60,000 in the Nou Camp in the last-16 of the Champions League. Five months later, on the Friday night before Southampton began their post-Spygate campaign still in the Championship, Ramsdale strolled out of the tunnel at Eastleigh's Silverlake Stadium for Saints Under 21s and their Premier League Cup opener against Blackburn. The official attendance was 246 and none of them paid to get in.

Ramsdale, who joined from Arsenal in a deal worth up to £25million after Saints' promotion in 2024, has not featured in a single matchday squad for Tonda Eckert this season. It was at Ramsdale's request that he played for the kids. He is now, this once Arsenal record goalkeeper signing and England international whose cumulative transfer fees hit almost £80m, seemingly fourth choice at second-tier Southampton.

Daniel Peretz, who arrived on loan from Bayern Munich last January and joined permanently this summer for around £6m, has been superb. He is now Eckert's No 1 and the Saints boss has made that clear to him. George Long, who also joined on loan while Ramsdale was at Newcastle last season before turning his stay permanent in June, has been told he's Eckert's No 2. Southampton also followed the recent trend of hiring an older third-choice keeper to help mentor the others so Ramsdale also finds himself behind 37-year-old Jamie Jones.

'That group worked really well together last year and this is the way that we will go forward,' said Eckert last week. He likes the unit. He likes the characters.

And that, really, is the nub of the predicament in which Ramsdale – and Saints - now find themselves. Southampton expected Ramsdale would leave in the summer and planned for his departure without really considering the prospect of him staying.

They have, as it stands, made a commitment to a new No 1 and Ramsdale, as he's shown before, is not a goalkeeper content to sit on the bench. Were he wired differently, Ramsdale could well have a Premier League winners' medal now. He was hugely popular at Arsenal among the players and staff, a big personality, and an early catalyst for getting the fans on board with Arteta's revolution.

The goalkeeper lives in Bournemouth with his wife Georgina (pictured together)

Aaron and Georgina are pictured on a summer family holiday together earlier this year

Ramsdale signed a long-term deal at Arsenal in May 2023 after which he declared he wanted to be their keeper for the next decade. 'I want to be a mainstay at this club and do special things, win trophies and see what this team can do,' he said at the time. 'Hopefully we can stay together for a number of years.'

Three months later they signed David Raya on loan and quickly, despite Arteta's protestations that he had 'no No 1s', took his place. Ramsdale was gutted. His dad said his son 'lost his smile'.

Arsenal's view was that, in Ramsdale, they had, as one insider put it, a 'f***ing good keeper and a great lad'. They just felt they had a better one in Raya. A year later, he was gone.

'If I was sitting on the bench, winning a trophy wouldn't have meant that much to me,' said Ramsdale after his move to Saints. 'I just wanted to play football. As a kid I wanted to play football, not to just sit on a bench.'

Right now, he's not even doing that. The question is whether that will change.

Eckert admitted last week he held 'honest conversations' with Ramsdale over the summer, though it is understood none of them involved telling Ramsdale the door is closed. The two are said to have a good relationship.

Ramsdale is seen arriving for Southampton training in July - carrying a big bag of tea

Now he is playing in front of just 246 fans - and none of them even paid to get in

Newcastle had the option of signing him after his loan spell last season. The Magpies spent around £4m on the loan fee to bring him in as competition for a faltering Nick Pope, with the view that Ramsdale was better with the ball at his feet, despite it being a figure that raised a few eyebrows among the Newcastle bean counters.

Ramsdale, again, became a much-loved figure among the squad - the stream of messages from his Newcastle team-mates on social media when he announced his return to Saints showed that - but when he got his chance on the pitch, he struggled to seize it.

While the public stance was that Ramsdale's future would be decided at the end of the season, there was a growing feeling internally as the campaign progressed that they would not be activating the option to buy him, especially as it's understood the figure to do so was well above the keeper's current market value.

RAMSDALE'S BIG TRANSFERS 2017: Sheffield United-Bournemouth (£1m) 2020: Bournemouth-Sheffield United (£18.5m) 2021: Sheffield United-Arsenal (£30m) 2024: Arsenal-Southampton (£25m) 2025: Southampton-Newcastle (loan - £4m)

No other moves materialised. Ramsdale made it clear he was keen to stay at Southampton, where he's a big character in the dressing room, and challenge for his place. His high wages are understood to be 'manageable' thanks to a relegation clause.

Ramsdale had enough of moving around clubs to what would be a fourth new side in three years so he only wanted to do so if the offer was too good to refuse and turned down interest throughout the window, including interest from Scotland, Spain and Germany.

Leeds had him firmly in their sights had their ambitious bid to bring in James Trafford not materialised and, had they failed to do so, would likely have landed him. A potential return to Bournemouth, where he lives, was also floated but the Cherries eventually plumped for Juventus keeper Michele Di Gregorio on loan.

Newcastle spent around £4m on the loan fee but didn't make the move permanent

Ramsdale had little interest in moving abroad and a Premier League transfer didn't materialise

Ramsdale had little interest in a loan move abroad, with Serie A sides like Como and Torino also sniffing around him, after his wife recently gave birth to a baby girl, nor did he want to stay in the Championship, go to a big club as a No 2, or join a struggling Premier League side.

The stick that's often used to beat Ramsdale is that he has already suffered three top-flight relegations with three different teams: Bournemouth, Sheffield United and Southampton. At the first two, he was named player of the season despite the drop.

And yet, despite all the noise, Ramsdale was named in Saints' 25-man squad submitted to the Football League. Perhaps there is a future after all?

He trains with the group and has been more involved in recent weeks. There's also a feeling among those around the club that were Peretz to suffer injury, it's likely Eckert would parachute Ramsdale straight into his place.

Sources close to Ramsdale say the 28-year-old still believes he has a big part to play in getting Southampton back to the Premier League.

It may take time, but Ramsdale believes he'll get his chance. Sources described his current fourth-choice predicament as only 'circumstantial'. Ones, perhaps, he might still be able to change.

Sports.title: Ricky Hatton's parents recall final conversation before son's tragic death
Sports.content:
Ricky Hatton's parents recall final conversation before son's tragic death

Ricky Hatton, one of Britain's best-known boxers, passed away 12 months ago when was found hanged following a long battle with his mental health

View Image Ricky Hatton (left) and his parents Ray and Carol

Ricky Hatton's mum has expressed her gratitude at having the opportunity to tell her son she loved him just three days before he died.

‌



Hatton, one of Britain's most-loved boxers and a former world champion, passed away aged 46 last September, having battled with depression throughout his life. Hatton had been open in the past about his struggles with alcohol and drugs, and at the inquest into his death during March, the coroner concluded the official cause of death was hanging.

‌



Hatton also had a troubled relationship with mum Carol and dad Ray and went long spells without speaking to his parents. But his mum has revealed she had a chance encounter with her son days before his death. "I pulled up on the car park because I saw his car," she told ITV Granada Reports.

‌



"He asked if everything was okay. I said 'Yeah, everything's fine.' I said I'd like to see a bit more of him. I'm so glad [I got to see him] because nobody knows when it's the last time you're going to see somebody."

We take a look back at his life in the ring where Hatton was, for far too brief a time, simply untouchable, a ruthless, all-action machine who delivered body punches like a lumberjack wielding an axe. And we look back at his global super-fights. No other fighter could lure 30,000 fans to Las Vegas where Ricky faced legends Floyd Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao. Hatton – the fighter – was very, very special, and as a personality he was box-office. ‌



Hatton's dad added: "Carol told him to always remember how much we all love him. You tell your grandkids how much you love them, you tell your wife how much you love them but I think, especially with men, don't ever be afraid of getting hold of your son and telling him you love him."

Hatton had been planning to return to the ring and was due to fly to Dubai to attend a press conference the day after he took his own life. And his mum added: "He always used to do things that attracted attention. He wanted to make people laugh and smile.

"But they do say behind the biggest laugh and the biggest smile is the most pain. People who lose somebody are always saying 'What if? What if?' But nobody knows what goes on inside a person's mind. People say it's a selfish act but you don't know when that dark cloud comes.

"We will move forward because I know Richard will be looking down on his family. I really believe that. We have to move forward, living our lives, talking about him, remembering him and loving him."

Sports.title: Great North Run 2026: Biggest field in history with £500,000 charity goal in its sights
Sports.content:
Great North Run 2026: Biggest field in history with £500,000 charity goal in its sights

The Great North Run has raised more than £450m for charity since 1981, and that figure is likely to rise to half a billion pounds. The event already holds the world record as the biggest half marathon in history, and will set a new record this year.

View 5 Images This year's Great North Run is held on Sunday

The Great North Run will celebrate its 45th anniversary on Sunday with its biggest-ever field of 63,000 competitors.

‌



Organisers estimate it has raised more than £450m for good causes since 1981, and that figure is likely to reach to half a billion pounds in the next two years.

‌



The event already holds the world record from 2014 as the biggest half marathon in history, when 41,615 crossed the finishing line; it will set a new record this year.

‌



First staged in June 1981, the race was founded by ex-athlete Sir Brendan Foster, 78, after he was inspired by taking part in New Zealand's Round the Bays Race in 1979.

World Athletics Ultimate Championship set to be major money maker for British stars READ MORE :

Amy Hunt looking to add more titles at inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship READ MORE :

View 5 Images Great North Run founder Sir Brendan Foster was joined by North East Mayor Kim McGuinness to celebrate this year's Great North Run

Sir Brendan said: "It has been the biggest mass participation event in the UK for some time and we entered the Guinness Book of Records many years ago. This will be our biggest run yet. In around two years, the money raised for charities will hit the half-billion-pound mark."

‌



The former long-distance athlete said he is looking forward to England and Newcastle United star Dan Burn starting their biggest ever event on Sunday.

He is following in a fine Toon tradition after Kevin Keegan ran the first 1981 event in a top that was half in Newcastle United's colours and half in those of Sunderland.

View 5 Images Dan Burn is taking part in this year's race (Image: Newcastle United via Getty Images)

‌



Ruth Johnson, who works on the paediatric care ward of the Freeman Hospital in Newcastle, is running for the Children's Heart Unit Fund.

She told how Mirror campaigner Max Johnson, now 18, inspired her during her early days on the ward in the months before he had his heart transplant in 2017.

Max and his heart donor Keira Ball's story changed the law on organ donation in England following our 'Change the Law for Life' crusade.

‌



"He taught me and inspired me from the very start," she said. "It will be so emotional for me, thinking of all the incredible families and children on the ward. I will have a big smile all the way around."

View 5 Images Former Pride of Britain producer Matthew Cox aims to raise £100,000 for MND research

A former producer of the Mirror Pride of Britain awards is on a mission to raise £100,000 after being diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease last year.

‌



Matthew Cox, 47, will be pushed in a wheelchair by his sister Natalie Owen, 39, from Wales and brother Tomos Ashton-Cox, 30, from Essex, before he walks the last eight miles. He has already completed the London, Leeds and Wales marathons since his diagnosis and has raised almost £80,000.

He spent years helping tell the stories of inspirational people; he is now undertaking an extraordinary challenge and using his own experience to help others living with MND.

"I want to raise £100,000. I may have to speak to Brendan Foster to keep the roads open for me at the finish. But I will keep going with every last breath."

‌



Cliff Thornton, 79, of Ovington, Northumberland, is in the elite club of runners who has taken part in every single Great North Run. He vividly remembers the first one in 1981 when he ran in a pair of 'suede and plastic shoes' from British Home Stores.

But he soon became a keen runner, clocking a PB of 1hr 19mins, and won a competition for the best GNR run T-shirt picture when he and his family were pictured in the Alps.

"It has been an amazing experience for me," said the retired finance director.

‌



The Great Run Company, which runs the event, said the number of competitors aged 25 and under has almost doubled over the past five years, with more than 15% of entrants now falling into that age group.

View 5 Images Eilish McColgan, pictured here with Daily Mirror reporter Jeremy Armstrong, remembers running the junior version with her mum Liz, who won the Great North Run in 1992

Eilish McColgan, the Commonwealth Champion, and four time Olympian, recalled running the Great North Junior Run with her mum Liz, who won the race in 1992.

‌



She said: "I had never been in a race before and had not joined a running club. It was cold and wet, very British weather, but it was good fun and made me decided to join a club back in Dundee.

"I never thought that I would become a professional athlete and be here all these years later. My mum and dad have both done it. My little brother is doing it for the first time this year.

"It doesn't matter if you are elite, doing it for a Personal Best or running for charity, everyone covers those same 13.1 miles. It is the same route that I run and Mo Farah ran. The history of the Great North Run is quite unique, and that is why it is so iconic."

Sports.title: World Athletics Ultimate Championship set to be major money maker for British stars
Sports.content:
World Athletics Ultimate Championship set to be major money maker for British stars

With an overall prize pot of $10million for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship and $150,000 on offer for the winners of the individual event, there is the potential for those on form in Hungary to make a tidy penny over the next three days.

View 2 Images Image of the stadium for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship (Image: World Athletics)

Talking about money is about as vulgar as it gets for Brits but it was the subject on everybody’s lips at athletics’ lucrative new event in Budapest. With an overall prize pot of $10million for the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championship and $150,000 on offer for the winners of the individual event, there is the potential for those on form in Hungary to make a tidy penny over the next three days.

‌



And in a sport where money can often be tight, even for those at the pinnacle, it is little wonder that the prospect of a financial windfall is serving as motivation.

‌



Usain Bolt, the greatest sprinter to have ever lived, is one of those in town to watch the event. At his peak, he could potentially have walked away with nearly half a million had he triumphed over 100m, 200m and the 4x100m mixed relay, which will kick off proceedings on Friday evening.

‌



That fact had not passed him by, and while the value of being the world's most famous athlete means that he is not exactly strapped for cash, he welcomed the money on offer. He said: “It’s great to see track and field go in a different direction.

“I was having a conversation with Asafa (Powell) before I came here and we were talking about that same thing (the prize money) and we thought ‘jeez’, we missed out on this cash prize. I won a few championships and it still doesn’t add up to all the cash. I won a few championships and it still doesn’t add up to all the cash. So I think it’s big, it’s good for the sport, in incentivises athletes to come out and do their best, to show up and be ready. I’m sad I missed out on it but I’m happy for them.”

Mile world record-holder Josh Kerr is among the current athletes who have welcomed the bump in prize money, while Britain’s new sprint queen Amy Hunt pointed out that athletics can be an expensive sport at the top level. With her four European titles in Birmingham earlier this year, as well as her World Championship silver medal over 200m in Tokyo 12 months ago, Hunt is one of the faces of athletics in the UK.

‌



View 2 Images Josh Kerr of Team Great Britain (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

And while that means that she is able to base herself in Italy without any financial worries, she knows it is not the case for everyone. She said: “I think financial security is a very taboo topic, but it’s also a very human and a very real topic. We all need money every day to survive and live.

“I’m lucky enough that I’ve been kind of successful in the last two years and I’ve got to a place where I’m financially stable enough to live abroad on my own. But there are other athletes in that race who are maybe lower down on the world rankings and don’t have the international medals, and it’s actually a struggle every day for them.

‌



“Track isn’t a particularly expensive sport on the outside, but there’s so much travel that goes into this, and looking after your body. Even just buying clean food gets incredibly expensive. It’s cheaper and easier to just go to McDonald’s, but I won’t go to McDonald’s, so it’s about making sure everyone has the best opportunities. I’ve seen people who were on my career pathway coming up through the junior ranks pulling away because they didn’t have that financial support. So it’s great to see this innovation and it really inspires more money to be injected.”

As well as the money available, this event will see a host of innovation tested out, including a striking black infield, as well as a live draft for the 200m lanes, a new format for field events and the elimination of ties in vertical jumps – there will be no repeat of Mutaz Essa Barshim and Gianmarco Tamberi’s shared gold. World Athletics president Seb Coe hopes that these innovations could be adopted at World Championships and Olympics in future, as he anticipates a potentially thrilling competition which is bringing the world’s best athletes together in what is usually a down year in the Olympic cycle.

He said: “We want this championship to be an incubator for change. As a proud Sheffielder, I would call this a blast furnace, ultimately casting what our sport can look like going forward. We want to take some of those innovations into the World Championships and the Olympic Games.

Article continues below

“We know that our athletes are in peak condition, you only need to follow their journey through Diamond League this year and other events, to know that they are at the top of their game. We will see Olympic champions, we will see world champions, we will see the newly crowned Diamond League champions from last week in Brussels, freshly-minted world record holders and my goodness, this has been an extraordinary season for that. They are all hungry to compete.”

Sports.title: Barry McGuigan makes prediction for Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight in Las Vegas
Sports.content:
Barry McGuigan makes prediction for Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight in Las Vegas

Barry McGuigan previews this weekend's huge fight as Conor Benn takes on Ryan Garcia for the WBC welterweight belt in Las Vegas on Saturday night

View 2 Images Conor Benn and Ryan Garcia ahead of their fight (Image: Fanatics)

This is the biggest bout of Conor Benn’s career, a first world title fight against a marquee opponent in Las Vegas.

‌



It doesn’t come much better than sharing a ring with Ryan Garcia on the Strip for the WBC welterweight belt.

‌



The two assignments against Chris Eubank Jnr were high-profile, high-octane affairs framed by the rivalry associated with their famous fathers. But this is a new dimension and, hand on heart, I cannot with certainty pick a winner.

‌



Benn’s last bout against Regis Prograis was his first at welterweight in four years, having gone up to light-middle and then middle to take on Eubank Jnr.

New UK venue emerges to host Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

Coming back to 147 pounds is a monumental task after so long at the higher weight. Will Benn get his strength back, or enough of it, in the 24 hours after the weigh-in to deliver a performance? You can see how drained he looks on social media posts.

Garcia is coming from the other direction. Though he has been campaigning at welter in his last couple of fights, he started out at super-featherweight and is the smaller man.

‌



But he has carried the extra speed with him and his devastating left hook can still be a weapon, particularly early in the contest.

Benn always comes to fight, standing straight in front of you, which could play right into Garcia’s hands. Benn’s ability to absorb any early onslaught will be determined by how much strength remains after boiling himself down.

View 2 Images Benn is taking a huge step up in clash when he takes on Garcia in Las Vegas (Image: Fanatics)

‌



Garcia could hurt Benn early and get him out of there. Alternatively if Benn gets through the early rounds he is in the fight.

If you stay on Garcia, like Rolando Romero did last year, you get success. Benn is more explosive than Rolly, has better feet, but does he have the chin?

Garcia has mixed in much better company yet mostly at a lighter weight. He is also proven in this environment, a global superstar used to the pressure of the Big Show.

‌



Can Benn cope at this level? Apart from a tired Eubank Jnr he hasn’t campaigned in the same rarefied air.

He is also the away fighter against a fan favourite. The Vegas experience is unlike any other. The fight crowd is not necessarily made up of boxing devotees but punters just there for the occasion.

It’s a different vibe. Garcia thrives on it, a box-office star who will milk the crowd and use it to his advantage. That might just be his superpower, giving him enough of an edge to get the job done.

Sports.title: F1 news: Verstappen threatens to purposely crash into rival as Hamilton in showdown talks
Sports.content:
F1 news: Verstappen threatens to purposely crash into rival as Hamilton in showdown talks

All the latest F1 news as Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton hit the headlines in Madrid

View 3 Images Max Verstappen is preparing for a unique challenge (Image: Getty Images)

Following Kimi Antonelli's epic win at Monza, the F1 circus has moved on to the all-new Madring for the Spanish Grand Prix. The street track on the outskirts of Madrid is expected to be a huge test for drivers and cars alike.

‌



With walls lining the high-speed circuit, there will almost certainly be safety cars and potentially red flags. Antonelli has arrived in the Spanish capital on a high after incredibly rising from 19th on the grid - due to an engine penalty - to win his home race.

‌



The victory took him 66 points clear of Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the drivers' standings, with Lewis Hamilton a further 10 points back following a nightmare home race for Ferrari. Hamilton, who could only finish sixth, clashed with team-mate Charles Leclerc at the first corners, with the Monegasque then crashing out on the second lap.

‌



Ahead of a crucial weekend in the championship battle, here's a round-up of the latest F1 news…

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Verstappen threatens to crash

Max Verstappen has joked about deliberately crashing into a rival ahead of the unique challenge at Silverstone. Following the Spanish Grand Prix, the four-time world champion will headline a kart race featuring 100 other racers.

‌



Lewis Hamilton takes swipe at Ferrari and concedes defeat in F1 title bid READ MORE :

Charles Leclerc gives health update after Ferrari star's horror Italian GP crash READ MORE :

Verstappen, who cut his teeth in karting as a child, will start at the back of the 101-driver field and must overtake every single one to succeed. The grid will include F1 fans, influencers, gamers, Red Bull athletes and regular kart racers, with the action streaming on Disney+ on Wednesday, September 16.

Asked about going up a friend during the novel challenge ahead of the Spanish Grand Prix, a smiling Verstappen quipped: "He'd better move out of the way, otherwise I'm going to plough him into the barrier!" To laughs from gathered media, he added: "I'm being serious, he'd better move when I'm coming."

View 3 Images Verstappen has joked about crashing during the kart race (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

‌



Hamilton's showdown talks

Hamilton had held showdown talks with Leclerc to "quash" their fallout at Monza. The seven-time world champion accused his team-mate of pushing him off the track on the opening lap, while Leclerc originally placed the onus on both drivers for the flashpoint.

Straight after the race, Hamilton hit back by saying "there was no 'we' in it" and added that he "doesn't race dirty" as he laid the blame at Leclerc's door. But ahead of this weekend's action, Hamilton revealed he had spoken directly with Leclerc to iron out their grievances.

View 3 Images Lewis Hamilton has cleared the air with Charles Leclerc (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He said: "We sat face-to-face, just him and me, and talked about it. We were both honest and open and then we quashed it and moved on. That shows the maturity from him and it is healthy."

Hamilton added: "We are going to have different opinions but we came together to find a way forward, and that is the positive of where we have got to over the past 15 months or so. If you look at the history of the sport, this has happened before, so it is no biggie."

Meanwhile, Leclerc said: "After reviewing, we spoke with Lewis and I obviously know I went too far in turn two. But it definitely did not affect the good relationship we have and going forward."

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta fires back at Gabriel Jesus as row over bitter Arsenal transfer exit escalates
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta fires back at Gabriel Jesus as row over bitter Arsenal transfer exit escalates

Mikel Arteta's approach to offloading players in the summer transfer window has caused some friction, with Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli frozen out before leaving

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta felt he was fair with Gabriel Jesus (Image: Sky Sports)

Mikel Arteta has admitted he was "very surprised" to hear criticism from Gabriel Jesus over the way he was treated by Arsenal before leaving for Barcelona this summer.

‌



Jesus joined Barca for a fee in the region of £8.5million in the latter stages of the summer transfer window, having fallen behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres in the pecking order. He was part of a group of players who were moved on, along with Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Christian Norgaard, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson.

‌



The method by which Arteta went about offloading the unwanted players caused a stir, with club legend Ian Wright saying he felt "uncomfortable" over the way Martinelli was cast aside. Jesus was delighted to land on his feet at Barca, but says "nobody told me nothing" and he was made to train alone.

‌



Arteta prides himself on having a close relationship with his players and appeared hurt when the comments were put to him ahead of Arsenal's game against Sunderland on Saturday.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"Very surprised, to be fair especially because with Gabriel I had an individual talk in the dressing room," Arteta told reporters in his pre-match press conference. "I don't know what the words were said, it's fine.

"And the words that we used for each other, it was all about gratitude. So, I don't know, it's okay. Sometimes I understand when you have to deliver bad news or news that people don't expect

"Those things are reactive. Somebody has to be there to back up, if I have to be. I have to be. And I understand.

‌



"What is important is normally what happens three months later, six months later, when Trossard comes in, he's in the dressing room with all of us, the atmosphere and the relation you have. And thanks God so far, with all the players that they left, at some point their relationship has been really good. I hope that's the same case."

View 3 Images Gabriel Jesus has criticised the way Arsenal dealt with his exit (Image: Getty Images)

Speaking to SportyTV, Jesus had said: "So, the truth is, I was training, I did all the pre-season with Arsenal as normal. Obviously, I knew already that probably I would not play there or get many opportunities, but nobody told me nothing.

‌



"Well, I am a professional. Obviously I was training with the group. Then, from nothing, they put me to train away from the group.

"Well, I was training, I was doing my maximum to be ready if I have a chance to play at a high level again. Then, obviously, in the last week it was very quick.

View 3 Images Gabriel Martinelli also left Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty)

‌



"The work with Deco, the president of the club, and my agent was amazing. In one day, it was sure that I would have the opportunity to come (to Barcelona). I said yes, straight away, no matter what and I am so happy to be here."

Martinelli was sold to Al-Hilal for a club-record fee of £60m following a protracted and awkward few weeks in which he rejected a move to Turkey. Wright said Martinelli was "not being spoken to" and "doesn't know what's going on" when asked about why he felt the Brazilian deserved better treatment.

He added: "For him to be nowhere near it, just makes me feel a bit sad for him. I think he's done enough in this squad to be treated with a bit more respect than he's been treated at the moment."

Sports.title: Masters legend hits out at Rory McIlroy and accuses him of saying ‘strange things’
Sports.content:
Masters legend hits out at Rory McIlroy and accuses him of saying ‘strange things’

Rory McIlroy has admitted that he is to be selective over the events he will play as he balances family time.

View 2 Images rory McIlory has left Gary Player shocked by his comments. (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

Golf legend Gary Player had said he is ‘shocked’ by comments made by Rory McIlroy over his enthusiasm for the game. The Northern Irishman has taken part in just 14 events this year, defending his Masters’ title.

‌



He completed the career Grand Slam last year when he lifted the title for the first time. It means he became just the sixth player, and the first European to complete the feat.

‌



McIlroy has now admitted that he is becoming increasingly selective of the events he plays with. He is instead looking to find more of a balance and spend more time with his wife and daughter.

‌



Rory McIlroy left young girl in tears with what he did at Irish Open READ MORE :

LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as star players owed £33m free to leave READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

But it’s something that Player doesn’t understand, with the 90-year-old, believing that the success should only increase his motivation to win more.

Speaking to the Golf Supply , Player said: “I hear Rory with the best swing in the world saying, ‘Now I’ve won the Grand Slam, I don’t have the same desire to play a lot.’ Man, he should be saying, ‘I want to win another Grand Slam’. I’m shocked.

‌



“And then he says, ‘I don’t believe in hitting a lot of balls’. Well, that’s c***. If you hit a lot of balls, you build up determination, and it makes you work harder, makes your muscles better. He comes out with very strange things.”

McIlroy finished tied fourth in the Tour Championship, five behind winner Scottie Scheffler.

Speaking at the tournament, McIlroy admitted : “I think once you start to lose your enthusiasm to go to the course, it's time to take a break.

‌



“I've turned up to events that I haven't necessarily wanted to be there because I feel like I should be there, and I've never — like I never play my — like if I'm going to show up to a tournament, I want to perform at my best and play my best, and there's been times when I haven't done that.”

View 2 Images Rory McIlroy is currently competing in the Irish Open. (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

He added: “It's frustrating to me, but it's also at the same time like no one wants to see me just go through the motions and be out there.

‌



“I feel like — like this is my third week in a row. I rarely do that anymore. I feel like that's my limit, like if I had to tee it up again next week — like when the playoffs used to be four events instead of three, that to me is tough.

“I think the last time I played four in a row might have been in 2024, and in the fourth week, I was like I'm done. I'm never doing this again.

“Again, I'm 37. I've been at this, this is my 18th or 19th year as a pro. Maybe my fuse is a little shorter than it used to be.”

Sports.title: Ibiza Final Boss sets date for Jordan McCann boxing rematch
Sports.content:
Ibiza Final Boss sets date for Jordan McCann boxing rematch

Ibiza Final Boss will return to the boxing ring this weekend, and, provided he comes away unscathed, the social media star is itching to fight Jordan McCann for a second time

View Image Jordan McCann punches Ibiza Final Boss (Image: Getty Images)

Ibiza Final Boss hopes to rematch rival Jordan McCann under the Misfits Boxing banner before the end of the year.

‌



The Final Boss - real name Jack Kay - took on the Manchester rapper back in June. In a rather wild and bizarre contest, which saw both fighters gas out early, it was Kay who would go on to get his hand raised on points.

‌



Both men are set to compete on the Misfits card in Newcastle on Saturday night. The Final Boss will take on influencer Kellen Jenkins, while McCann will trade leather with Big Stacks in the main event. Providing both men come away relatively unscathed, Kay is itching for a sequel with his former rival.

‌



And it could come before the end of the year, with Kay targeting the rumoured December 5th showcase in Manchester. "Hopefully me and Jordan (McCann) can run it back. I heard the next Misfits card is in Manchester in December (5th). So, hopefully me and Jordan can run it back. Round two," he said at the pre-fight press conference on Thursday evening. McCann was eager to accept Kay's demands, stating: "1 million per cent."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
