Tech.title: You Can Now Buy the Trump Phone for $250 More Than Originally Priced
Tech.content:
After Apple’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, which debuted the long-rumored foldable iPhone Duo with a starting price of $1,999, the conversation at my home has mainly centered on our mobile phone expenses and whether it’s worth upgrading.

Well, good news: There is a flashy phone on the market that is cheaper than the hyped-up foldable. OK, there are many well below that price, but do they operate on an outdated operating system? Are they painted gold?

Ring the alarms and throw the confetti; I am talking about Trump Mobile’s golden T1 Phone.



The gold-colored mobile device was originally priced at an affordable $499. Due to a quiet price hike the provider implemented overnight, as first reported by The Verge, the Trump phone is now marked at $749. That’s a $250 increase, making the T1 a more expensive option over the iPhone 17E. Control your excitement.

A Trump Mobile spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

Trump Mobile didn’t explain the cost increase, but the writing has been on the wall for some time. The company’s execs went on record earlier this year with The Verge that the initial $499 price tag was a temporary introductory price. It’s even possible for the T1 to become more expensive, with a price of up to $999 in the future. So, you know, embrace this price while you can.

That said, the company didn’t provide any firm explanation beyond that, leading us to speculate that this could be due to the ongoing global memory chip shortage driven by the AI boom, known as RAMageddon. Apple recently implemented an array of price hikes due to the RAM shortage, upping the price of its older iPhone lineup, iPads, MacBooks and more.

But the Trump phone isn’t in the same ballpark as an iPhone. In fact, the Trump phone is essentially a reskinned mid-level HTC handset.

This might be the worst possible shade of gold. Corinne Reichert/CNET

After an almost year-long delay, the Android phone, originally advertised as made in the US, began shipping in May to members of the media, which included CNET (you can read the full review here), along with a few customers (who paid a preorder deposit of $100 for the device).

Once CNET’s experts were able to take a closer look at the T1, which is now labeled as being “assembled in the USA,” we confirmed what iFixit learned before us: The Trump phone was likely manufactured in Guangdong, China, and is nearly identical to the Taiwanese HTC U24 Pro. The latter handset was released to market two years ago and can be found for less than $600 at retailers such as Walmart and Amazon.

But are those HTC handsets I mentioned above painted gold? Do they come equipped with Truth Social on an outdated OS, while their casings are decorated with an American flag missing some stripes? I think not.

So, if you’re still in the market for Trump Mobile’s T1 phone, I advise you to get while the getting’s good. Before we know it, the Trump phone could be priced at around $1,000. I’m all for retro tech and nostalgia, but for all the outdated tech this phone is built on, that price tag is pushing it when newer phones on the market, sporting more impressive bells and whistles, are clocking in at a price that’s way lower.

Tech.title: Jell-O and Beer May Hold the Keys to Brewing Houses on Mars
Tech.content:
Establishing life on another planet is a multifaceted process with many problems. Housing is one major challenge, but a new study suggests researchers have found a way to build living quarters on Mars using materials already present on the planet, along with a couple of other clever ingredients.

The study, published on Sept. 10 in the journal Chem Circularity, reports that researchers found a way to turn the sand on Mars into what is functionally low-grade concrete using little more than gelatin, yeast, and the natural Martian environment. Combine the three ingredients, and the dry, cold, low-pressure environment of Mars freeze-dries the mixture, turning it into a porous, foam-like material strong enough to build houses on the red planet.

“My inspiration came from freeze-dried fruits that become harder,” senior author Jishen Qiu of The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology said in a statement. “So, I asked myself if we can take advantage of that and make some materials.”

According to Qiu, the concrete produced by this method measures 10 to 12 megapascals (a metric unit of pressure), putting it on par with low-grade concrete here on Earth. This concrete is strong enough to build a one- or two-story house on Earth, and since Earth has three times the gravity of Mars, it’s more than strong enough to build structures on Mars too.

The gelatin is run-of-the-mill porcine gelatin, which means it’s made from pigs, and it’s quite literally the same stuff that Jell-O uses to make its jiggly dessert. For the yeast, Qiu created a specially engineered version covered in the same proteins mussels use to attach themselves to rocks. These two ingredients, along with pounded-up Martian rocks and water, create the material.

Mars’ frigid cold, low-pressure environment effectively freeze-dries the material, causing water to sublimate, which means it turns directly from a solid to a vapor, leaving the Martian concrete behind. Because this process is so fast, items must be 3D-printed in real time to work properly.

The team tested it by 3D printing two small beehive-shaped structures about the size of a wine cork in a simulated Martian environment, but the team believes the process can scale up. Once the structures have reached the end of their usefulness, people on Mars can break them down, mix them in a bioreactor, and brew a new building with the same materials, as long as there’s still yeast alive to reproduce.

An elegant solution to a long-standing problem

Houses on Mars made with this method would resemble beehives, but be made of what is essentially concrete. Nin Liu

Delivering humans to Mars is already a tall order. Elon Musk tried to get it done by 2025 and missed the mark by at least a decade. However, getting people there is only half the battle. Once there, they need a place to live that can withstand the Martian environment, which includes temperature swings of nearly 100 degrees Celsius and virtually no radiation protection from the sun due to the thin Mars atmosphere.

There are many ideas about the subject, ranging from inflatable domiciles to the idea of letting self-propagating fungi grow whole buildings. Some enterprising scientists from the Indian Space Research Organisation even made space bricks from Martian soil, guar gum, urea, nickel chloride and a bacterium called Sporosarcina pasteurii, which converts urea and calcium into calcite. This lets the soil harden into something resembling concrete.

NASA held a habitat challenge from 2015 to 2019 that tasked companies and researchers to 3D-print homes using unique methods and materials. The winners took home over $2 million in prizes. In short, no stone has been left unturned, and people are using all sorts of exotic materials to try to find the best solution for habitats on Mars, including Qiu.

“I always ask myself: Is there any physical law or fundamental mechanism that prevents us from doing this?” Qiu said. “I can’t see any at this point in time. We are confident in scaling it up. It would surprise me if materials for future Martian engineering will not be as diverse as those used in Earth engineering, and biology will certainly contribute.”

Tech.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra: The Highest-End Phones Compared
Tech.content:
Apple’s $1,299 iPhone 18 Pro Max now stands tall as the company’s newest nonfolding high-end flagship phone. Announced at the company’s Surprise and Shine event on Wednesday, it packs big camera and battery upgrades. But with a starting price that’s $100 higher than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, the phone’s 256GB model is now priced closely to Samsung’s $1,300 Galaxy S26 Ultra.

While every iPhone received a $100 price increase that’s likely influenced by the ongoing RAM shortage, Apple’s topline iPhone appears to be a close rival to the S26 Ultra in several key areas, especially when it comes to battery life and cameras.

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra design and display

While Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max and Samsung’s Galaxy S26 Ultra are big phones, their design aesthetics are quite different. The 18 Pro Max sports a similar aluminum unibody design to the one that debuted on last year’s 17 Pro Max. It comes in burgundy red, glacier blue, silver and black colors. Its shape gives it a hefty appearance, but one that fits in well when the phone is being used as a professional camera for events like Apple TV’s Major League Baseball broadcasts. And at 249 grams (8.8 ounces), the 18 Pro Max isn’t lightweight by any stretch. The phone has a 6.8-inch OLED display that should be quite expansive for videos, websites and games.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra has a slightly bigger 6.9-inch AMOLED display, but at 214 grams, it’s notably lighter than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. It also comes in six colors: pink gold, silver shadow, cobalt violet, sky blue, white and black. The S26 Ultra is also the thinnest in its line, but its Privacy Display is its most unique feature. The S26 Ultra’s display can make specific apps or notifications difficult to see from off-angle viewing, making it easier to hide content from prying eyes without needing to apply a privacy screen protector. No other company has replicated Samsung’s Privacy Display, which does make the phone stand out.

The iPhone 18 Pro Max in glacier blue. Apple/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra battery capacity

Both phones have big batteries. While Apple doesn’t disclose its battery specs in the US — instead citing that it can play 45 hours of video — its Ireland website claims the physical SIM edition will have a 5,391-mAh capacity. That’s slightly higher than the 5,000-mAh capacity on the S26 Ultra and might be even higher on the eSIM model that will be sold in the US.

Apple hasn’t yet disclosed the charging speed for the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but this is an area where Samsung already excels — the S26 Ultra has 60-watt wired charging and won our CNET Lab Test award for fastest wired charging phone by recharging from 0% to 76% in 30 minutes. That said, last year’s iPhone 17 Pro Max had a 40-watt charging speed that was one of our top performers, recharging 0% to 69% in the same 30-minute test. We look forward to testing out the 18 Pro Max to see how it fares.

You can turn on Privacy Display in Quick Settings to prevent others from seeing what’s on your screen. Celso Bulgatti/CNET

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra cameras

Both phones also have their respective companies’ highest-end cameras, with Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Max now featuring a variable-aperture camera that can physically open or close to take better photos in darker or lighter environments. This feature comes with the Pro Max’s three-camera setup that includes a 49-megapixel wide camera, a 48-megapixel ultrawide camera and a 48-megapixel telephoto camera with a 4x optical zoom. While the S26 Ultra doesn’t include a variable aperture, it has four cameras on the back that include a 200-megapixel main camera, a 50-megapixel ultrawide, a 50-megapixel telephoto with a 5x optical zoom and a 10-megapixel telephoto with a 3x optical zoom.

iPhone 18 Pro Max vs. Galaxy S26 Ultra processor, features

Apple’s A20 Pro processor powers the company’s latest AI features, headlined by the new Siri AI assistant that is built with Apple’s collaboration with Google’s Gemini. It can help you look up specific information buried in your emails and texts and turn them into actionable items like new reminders or calendar events. Apple also made a point of showing off the A20 Pro’s gaming abilities and how the phone’s vapor chamber helps keep it running cool while pushing intensive graphics.

But Samsung’s phone includes Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Gen 5 for Galaxy processor, powering its own slate of Galaxy AI features focused on proactive suggestions, along with photo editing. It’s also quite capable of high-end gaming.

Check out the specs below to compare both phones further.

Tech.title: Apple Hikes iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max Prices by $100
Tech.content:
Planning to scoop up a new iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone 18 Pro Max after watching the Apple event this week? Hope you have an extra $100 in your pocket. Apple confirmed at Wednesday’s live Surprise and Shine event that the two phones will cost $100 more than the previous versions. The iPhone 18 Pro will start at $1,199 and the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max will begin at $1,299. Both of those prices include 256GB of storage.

Both phones will be available for preorder this Saturday, Sept. 12, and will launch on Sept. 18.

The price increase was expected, and was actually lower than some observers predicted. The $100 price hike matches Samsung’s cost hikes for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Flip 8, and Google’s hikes with the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro.

Andrew Lanxon, CNET editor-at-large, notes that the new phones are packed with Apple’s latest tech, including upgraded cameras, new A20 Bionic processors, and fresh colors, including a much-buzzed-about dark cherry, labeled burgundy.
